articles.title: Ngumoha emerges as potential Mo Salah replacement with winner as Liverpool beat Wrexham
articles.summary: Liverpool are short of right-sided wingers but Rio Ngumoha showed his versatility by playing there, and scoring, against Wrexham
articles.content:
Ngumoha emerges as potential Mo Salah replacement with winner as Liverpool beat Wrexham

Liverpool are short of right-sided wingers but Rio Ngumoha showed his versatility by playing there, and scoring, against Wrexham

Last Update:

Rio Ngumoha suggested he could be the answer to Liverpool’s right-sided problem with the only goal as Andoni Iraola maintained his 100% start as Reds boss with a 1-0 victory over Wrexham in New York.

Liverpool are believed to be in talks with Paris Saint-Germain over the signing of Bradley Barcola, who would add another option on the left wing alongside Cody Gakpo, Hugo Ekitike, Florian Wirtz and new signing Victor Munoz.

Ngumoha is also comfortable on the left but came on at half-time last night and operated from the opposite flank – a position that has been filled by Mohamed Salah in recent years – and showed his versatility with a bright display that was capped with a goal, albeit a scruffy one with a huge deflection taking the ball into the net.

The 17-year-old told the club’s official website: “I just want to play and start as many games as I can. These games are a really good showcase to show the manager, because it’s a fresh start for everyone. It’s really important and it’s good.

“All the coaching staff are just telling me to play my normal game really, whether that’s going inside or outside. I’ve been working on it in training anyway, playing on the right and the left. Just being unpredictable really.”

Table of Contents

Nyoni also impresses for Liverpool

Iraola named a young side with Alexander Isak, Florian Wirtz, Ryan Gravenberch and Jeremy Jacquet all remaining in Chicago. And that allowed Trey Nyoni to showcase his talents once again after an impressive showing in the 4-2 win over Sunderland on Saturday.

Iraola said: “Trey is very good on the ball, very calm, he reads the situations well. We’re forcing him in the work without the ball, in the press, and he is absolutely doing very well. I think the timings of the jumps are very good. He is always confident on the ball so we encourage him. Sometimes even if he loses the ball, ‘Try to find the No.10, try to find the No.9, even balls in behind, look a little bit further’ because he can do it, because he is so good.

“At the end, he is a midfielder who, I always say, you have to ask for the ball sometimes with pressure – and he doesn’t feel this pressure. Even when he has one opponent quite close, he asks for that ball and he’s confident, he doesn’t rush. For me, that is very valuable.”

It was another useful outing overall for Liverpool, who play Leeds next on Sunday.

“I think overall we were more solid than the other day,” added Iraola. “It was a different kind of game, the pitch is quite narrow and there are not a lot of spaces. But I think we had good spells. And even if the other day maybe you score more goals and it looks nicer, I think today we were more a team and more collective.

“We are sometimes arriving late, but I think it’s a step forward, since especially the first half against Sunderland. That is more of a reference than the second half. Slowly, slowly I hope every game we are closer and closer. We start to add new bodies, because now we are playing with a lot of the young players. Slowly, slowly we have to add the senior players that are starting to train with us, so we can arrive to the beginning of the season in a good place.”

Big-name quartet to return for Liverpool against Leeds

Liverpool should have more players available at the weekend with Jacquet expected to make his Reds debut following his summer switch from Rennes.

Iraola said: “Yes, my idea is for Ryan, for Florian, for Alex, for even Jeremy Jacquet to have their first minutes against Leeds. We’ll see how many minutes they can play but we have to start slowly, slowly integrating more of the senior players that have had less training sessions. I think they should be ready on the weekend to have their first minutes.”

articles.title: CAF to ‘assess and evaluate’ Infantino’s controversial World Cup proposals
articles.summary: CAF responded very differently to UEFA and other confederations.
articles.content:
CAF to ‘assess and evaluate’ Infantino’s controversial World Cup proposals

CAF responded very differently to UEFA and other confederations.

Last Update:

The Confederation of African Football (CAF) has notably elected not to criticise FIFA president Gianni Infantino’s plans to sell stakes in the World Cup to private investors, saying it will “assess and evaluate” the proposals.

There has been outrage across world football after FIFA confirmed the plans on Tuesday.

Under Infantino’s proposed scheme, a company, FIFA Forward Enterprise (FFE), would be put together to oversee FIFA’s top competitions in the men’s and women’s games, including the World Cup and the Club World Cup. The plan could see Infantino earn tens of millions and raise the possibility of the World Cup and Club World Cup being held more often than every four years.

FIFA’s 211 member associations would receive a stake that they could either keep or sell to generate income. It is claimed that Infantino, set to be re-elected unopposed until 2031, would be positioned to become commissioner of the company after his final term as president comes to a close. It is expected he could command a salary akin to that of NFL commissioner Roger Goodell, who earns $64m annually.

A majority stake in the company would be owned by FIFA, with private investors taking on around 20 to 30 per cent and the member nations each receiving a small stake. Joshua Kushner — brother of Donald Trump’s son-in-law Jared — is the proposed lead investor.

Infantino subsequently contacted all 211 member associations, giving them extra incentive to back the plan.

He has told the members they will receive $40m (£30m) if they support the proposals, adding that £20m will be immediately available to them on January 1 next year and giving the associations a deadline of September 19 by which to accept to the one-time offer.

European football’s governing body UEFA has vehemently criticised the plans, saying they cross “a line that football’s governing institutions should never cross”. The AFC and CONCACAF have each criticised the lack of proper process, while former FIFA president Sepp Blatter has said the governing body risks “losing its soul” if the plans are implemented.

However, CAF, which oversees a host of smaller member associations that would stand to be among the biggest beneficiaries from the proposed scheme, responded in a very different way.

A CAF statement read: “The Confederation Africaine de Football (“CAF“) received correspondence today from FIFA on the proposed FIFA Forward Enterprise initiative, in accordance with the consultation process that is currently underway with FIFA Member Associations and the FIFA Council.

“As part of this consultation process, the CAF President, Dr Patrice Motsepe, will host a meeting of the CAF Executive Committee next week, to inter-alia, assess and evaluate the proposed FIFA Forward Enterprise initiative.

“CAF also encourages its Member Associations to examine the FIFA Forward Enterprise proposal and participate in the consultation process in accordance with CAF and FIFA’s regulations and established procedures.

“CAF is committed to continue consulting and working together with its Member Associations, FIFA, other Football Confederations and stakeholders in support of increasing financial and other resources for the development and growth of football in Africa and worldwide.”

articles.title: Newcastle suffer friendly defeat at Bristol City as defensive issues laid bare
articles.summary: The Magpies' third pre-season game did not go to plan.
articles.content:
Newcastle suffer friendly defeat at Bristol City as defensive issues laid bare

The Magpies' third pre-season game did not go to plan.

Last Update:

Newcastle United suffered a pre-season humbling as the Premier League side were beaten 4-1 by Championship Bristol City at Ashton Gate on Wednesday.

The Magpies, who have seen two key players sold this summer in the form of Anthony Gordon and Sandro Tonali, were without all but one of their players who featured at the World Cup, with Anthony Elanga the sole exception.

New signings Aladji Bamba and Bazoumana Toure did not feature, while captain Bruno Guimaraes — who is reportedly keen to move to Arsenal — is not due to return to training until Friday after his exertions with Brazil in North America.

Still, even with the likes of Tino Livramento, Malick Thaw, Dan Burn, Lewis Miley, Yoane Wissa, Will Osula and Nick Woltemade also out of the squad, manager Eddie Howe will have been far from pleased with the performance.

Table of Contents

Murphy and Botman struggle as Newcastle beaten

Newcastle went close early through Sean Neave, before Bristol took the lead when a fine free-kick from Sam Greenwood flew in off the crossbar.

It was 2-0 when Lorent Tolaj fired past Ewen Jaouen, though he appeared to get away with a foul in the build-up on Newcastle defender Sven Botman, who endured a chastening evening.

Max Bird made it 3-0 with a low finish five minutes into the second half after makeshift right-back Jacob Murphy casually conceded possession, with his efforts in tracking back thereafter leaving a lot to be desired.

Harvey Barnes, fresh from signing a new long-term contract, pulled one back with a low finish from a Jacob Ramsey lay-off after Matheos Ferreira won the ball high up the pitch.

But a disappointing night was capped by an own goal from Botman as the centre-back inadvertently turned a left-wing cross beyond Nick Pope, his struggles and those of Murphy highlighting the need for Newcastle to add at full-back and at the heart of the defence in a transfer window that has already seen them make four signings.

Ipswich lose to Osasuna, Lookman doubles up for Atleti

Meanwhile, Newcastle’s Premier League rivals Ipswich Town suffered a 2-1 home defeat to LaLiga side Osasuna.

Miguel Auria gave Osasuna the lead before Chuba Akpom equalised for Gary O’Neil’s men.

But Osasuna clinched victory 10 minutes from time as Raul Moro found the net with a fierce strike from outside the box.

An all-LaLiga friendly saw Atletico Madrid continue their preparations with a 4-1 win over Getafe.

Ademola Lookman was on target twice for Diego Simeone’s men, whose final two pre-season games come against Manchester United and Manchester City.

articles.title: FIFA would ‘lose its soul’ under controversial World Cup scheme, Blatter warns
articles.summary: Blatter has joined the chorus of dissenting voices.
articles.content:
FIFA would ‘lose its soul’ under controversial World Cup scheme, Blatter warns

Blatter has joined the chorus of dissenting voices.

Last Update:

Sepp Blatter has warned that FIFA will lose its soul if it implements a controversial plan to sell stakes in the World Cup to private investors.

There has been outrage across world football after FIFA confirmed the plans on Tuesday.

Under the scheme, a company, FIFA Forward Enterprise (FFE), would be put together to oversee FIFA’s top competitions in the men’s and women’s games, including the World Cup and the Club World Cup. The plan could see FIFA president Gianni Infantino earn tens of millions and raise the possibility of the World Cup and Club World Cup being held more often than every four years.

FIFA’s 211 member associations would receive a stake that they could either keep or sell to generate income. In addition, it is claimed that Infantino, set to be re-elected unopposed until 2031, would be positioned to become commissioner of the company after his final term as president comes to a close. It is expected he could command a salary of $64m as commissioner.

A majority stake in the company would be owned by FIFA, with private investors taking on around 20 to 30 per cent and the member nations each possessing a small stake. Joshua Kushner — brother of Donald Trump’s son-in-law Jared — is the proposed lead investor.

Infantino has subsequently written to all 211 member associations, giving them extra incentive to back the plan.

He has told the members they will receive $40m (£30m) if they support the plan, adding that £20m will be immediately available to them on January 1 next year.

However, Infantino gave those members a deadline of September 19 by which to accept to the one-time offer.

European football’s governing body UEFA has vehemently criticised the plans, saying they cross “a line that football’s governing institutions should never cross”.

And former FIFA president Blatter, who resigned in 2015 amid a corruption probe and was subsequently banned for eight years by the body’s ethics committee, has joined the chorus of dissenting voices.

“Football belongs to no individual and to no institution. It ⁠belongs to the people,” Blatter told Reuters.

“If FIFA were transferred into a profit-oriented corporate structure, ​it would lose its soul.”

Blatter has criticised his successor on numerous occasions, slamming the decision to expand the World Cup to 48 teams, the award of the 2034 tournament to Saudi Arabia and the suspension of United States forward Folarin Balogun’s ban for a last-16 tie with Belgium at this year’s competition after apparent influence by US president Donald Trump.

“The FIFA World Cup is not a commercial asset ​that belongs to a ​handful of executives,” Blatter added. “It is part of the cultural heritage of world football. FIFA is the guardian of the World Cup, not its owner. There is a ​fundamental difference.

“The beneficiaries should be the game itself — from grassroots football to the highest international ​level — not outside investors seeking returns.”

articles.title: BREAKING: Bournemouth forward Kroupi set for at least three months out after foot surgery
articles.summary: It is a huge blow to new Bournemouth boss Marco Rose.
articles.content:
BREAKING: Bournemouth forward Kroupi set for at least three months out after foot surgery

It is a huge blow to new Bournemouth boss Marco Rose.

Last Update:

Bournemouth forward Eli Junior Kroupi is set to miss three to four months after undergoing foot surgery.

Kroupi, who enjoyed a stunning first season in the Premier League, had been linked with the likes of Barcelona, Paris Saint-Germain and Tottenham.

But any hope of a transfer for the 20-year-old is over for now after The Athletic’s David Ornstein reported Kroupi is facing a lengthy spell on the sidelines.

Kroupi reportedly sustained the injury during Bournemouth’s pre-season trip to Austria. He travelled back to England for treatment before having surgery on Wednesday.

Bournemouth had stood firm amid significant interest in Kroupi, making it clear they had no desire to sell him.

But the Cherries now face being without him until October or November in a significant blow to new boss Marco Rose.

Kroupi injury leaves big void for Bournemouth

Kroupi joined Bournemouth from Lorient in February 2025 but spent the remainder of the 2024-25 campaign on loan at the Ligue 1 club.

He starred in his debut Premier League campaign as Bournemouth qualified for the Europa League in what proved to be Andoni Iraola’s final season in charge.

Kroupi was Bournemouth’s top scorer last term with 13 goals in 2025-26, all of which came in the Premier League.

While Bournemouth still have Evanilson to play through the middle of their attack, Kroupi’s injury increases the pressure on the likes of Rayan, Justin Kluivert and Marcus Tavernier to contribute goals as they attempt to hit the ground running under Rose while competing on two fronts.

Antoine Semenyo, who left for Manchester City in January, was second behind Kroupi for Bournemouth last season with 10 goals. Tavernier scored eight, Evanilson netted six, while Rayan contributed five. Kluivert, who dealt with injury for much of the season, scored twice.

Bournemouth could still lose one of their stars to another club. Alex Scott has been linked with a host of Premier League clubs and is said to be champions Arsenal’s alternative midfield target if they fail to prise Bruno Guimaraes from Newcastle.

Rose takes charge of his first official game as Bournemouth boss on August 23, when they open the season away at Manchester City.

articles.title: “I’m here to bring Italy back” – Mancini promises glorious return
articles.summary: Mancini steered Italy to the Euros title in 2021
articles.content:
“I’m here to bring Italy back” – Mancini promises glorious return

Mancini steered Italy to the Euros title in 2021

Last Update:

Roberto Mancini has set out to win a major trophy once again with Italy as he starts a second stint in charge of the national team.

Former Manchester City boss Mancini, 61, won the delayed Euro 2020 title against England at Wembley.

But he left in 2023 after failing to reach the 2022 World Cup and shockingly inherits an Italian side who have now missed three World Cups in a row.

“I’m here to bring Italy back to where it deserves to be,” he said at his unveiling.

“Regardless of what happened in 2023, the goal is always to win and play well. I’m convinced the players are there and that they’re good, especially the young ones.

“I’d like to win a major trophy, maybe even two. I’d like to build a project with the national team.”

Italy have won four World Cups but have failed to make it past the group stage since their most recent title in 2006.

Mancini will first have to qualify for the Euros back in England in 2024 before hoping to end that long wait for a return on the global stage.

He said: “If Italy qualified for the World Cup, as would be normal, they would still be a team aspiring to reach the final, even if they weren’t among the favourites.

“We want to become a team to beat: now we’ll prepare for the European Championship and then we’ll think about the World Cup.”

Mancini’s first game in charge will be a Nations League match against Belgium in September.

articles.title: BREAKING: FIFA charges Argentina players over World Cup final conduct and opens case over Falklands banner
articles.summary: Argentina's conduct after the semi-final and proved extremely controversial.
articles.content:
BREAKING: FIFA charges Argentina players over World Cup final conduct and opens case over Falklands banner

Argentina's conduct after the semi-final and proved extremely controversial.

Last Update:

FIFA has charged several Argentina players for their conduct in the aftermath of their World Cup final defeat to Spain and opened proceedings against the country’s Football Association for the display of a banner relating to the Falkland Islands after the semi-final win over England.

Spain lifted the trophy for the second time in their history after an uninspiring final was settled by Ferran Torres’ extra-time strike.

Ugly scenes followed at the end, with several Spain players accosted by Argentina counterparts. Leandro Paredes was at the centre of the controversy, as he grabbed Eric Garcia by the throat before pushing Gavi to the turf.

FIFA confirmed on Wednesday it had levelled three charges for assault against Paredes, while also charging Nahuel Molina (two counts, one completed and one attempted) and assistant coach Roberto Ayala (one count). Ayala was involved in confrontation with Spain’s Dani Olmo and promised to apologise in person to the Barcelona star.

Nahuel Molina (one count) and Thiago Almada (one count) have also been charged for unsporting behaviour, as has Spain midfielder Gavi (one count).

FIFA added that those accused would have the opportunity to present their position before a decision by the disciplinary committee.

In addition, the Argentinian Football Association (AFA) looks set to face action for the team’s actions after La Albiceleste came from behind to beat England 2-1 in the semi-final.

Amid the celebrations, several Argentina players posed with a banner that read  “Las Malvinas son Argentinas (The Falklands are Argentine).”

Britain and Argentina went to war over the Falklands in 1982, with the 74-day conflict resulting in the deaths of 649 Argentine soldiers, 255 British combatants and three civilians. The Falklands remain a British controlled territory, though Argentina insists the archipelago in the South Atlantic is its possession.

A formal investigation was demanded by the British government, and a case has been opened against the AFA for the team “using a sports event for demonstrations of a non-sporting nature”.

The proceedings against the AFA also relate to “team misconduct” “discrimination and racist abuse” and “order and security at matches”.

The FIFA statement read: “The FIFA Disciplinary Committee has opened proceedings against the Argentinian Football Association for potential breaches of article 13 paragraph 2 c) (Using a sports event for demonstrations of a non-sporting nature), article 14 paragraph 5 (Team misconduct), article 15 (Discrimination and racist abuse) and article 17 (Order and security at matches) of the FIFA Disciplinary Code in light of discriminatory chants and gestures, late kick-offs, failure to comply with match and security protocols, the display of inappropriate messages by the team and spectators and the throwing of objects by spectators in relation to several matches of the representative team of Argentina at the FIFA World Cup 2026.”

articles.title: ‘I would like him to stay’ – but De Zerbi won’t guarantee Tottenham midfielder Bergvall a starting place
articles.summary: Will the Swede stay with Spurs?
articles.content:
‘I would like him to stay’ – but De Zerbi won’t guarantee Tottenham midfielder Bergvall a starting place

Will the Swede stay with Spurs?

Last Update:

Tottenham manager Roberto De Zerbi says he wants midfielder Lucas Bergvall to stay at the club and develop into a ‘top player’ but will not promise the Sweden international a starting role.

De Zerbi has spent big this summer in recruiting Sandro Tonali from Newcastle and Mateus Fernandes from London rivals West Ham.

That has seemingly pushed Bergvall, 20, down the pecking order and he has been linked with moves to Newcastle and Nottingham Forest.

Bergvall started as Spurs’ pre-season continued with a penalty shootout win in Sydney and De Zerbi said after the game that his midfielder’s future remains unclear.

“I’m always being very clear with him and with you. I would like that he stays with us,” said De Zerbi.

“I think he’s potentially a top, top, top player. But then I don’t want to convince anyone to stay. Tottenham is already, without me, a top club and we are not to convince anyone to stay.

“He can find the space if he stays with us. The competition within the players will be very strong because we are Tottenham and we have to build a strong squad – not just 11 players – especially considering a lot of injuries we suffered in the last two, three seasons.

“Football is going in a clear direction – to compete for the highest places in the table, you have to manage 22, 23, 24 players. I don’t want 24, but 21, 22 of a high level.”

Bergvall started in a deeper midfield role in Sydney alongside Archie Gray, a position it is reported that he facours. But De Zerbi has doubts over his ability to play there.

De Zerbi continued: “He wants space. He wants to play as a double pivot as a position. I can’t give, for any player in the world, their place in the first XI guaranteed.

“I want to be honest with the players. I want to be clear. I don’t want to make the first mistake. In terms of position, I can’t give a guarantee. It’s right when he wants to play as a central midfielder.

“But to play as a central midfielder, sometimes it is to attack, sometimes to keep the holder, to move the ball faster. He has to improve.”

articles.title: Henderson has Brentford contract terminated as he closes in on move to Chelsea
articles.summary: Chelsea have edged closer to the surprise signing of Jordan Henderson after the England midfielder left Brentford
articles.content:
Henderson has Brentford contract terminated as he closes in on move to Chelsea

Chelsea have edged closer to the surprise signing of Jordan Henderson after the England midfielder left Brentford

Last Update:

Jordan Henderson has left Brentford ahead of his anticipated move to Chelsea.

The 36-year-old spent just 12 months at the Gtech Community Stadium, making 34 appearances for the Bees after joining from Ajax, but has now had his contract terminated.

That paves the way for a move across London to Stamford Bridge with Chelsea boss Xabi Alonso eager to add some experience to a young squad.

Henderson is renown for his professional attitude and Alonso is hoping that influence will inspire a group that limped to 10th in the Premier League last season.

The England international told Brentford’s official website: “I leave Brentford with a lot of gratitude for the opportunity the club gave me, and for the support and care shown to me and my family from day one.

“Coming back to the Premier League was really important to me, and Brentford gave me that chance. I’ll always be thankful for that.

“I hope I was able to play my part in helping the team through an important period for the club. We achieved a lot together last season, and it’s something everyone involved should be proud of.

“Brentford is a special football club. It’s ambitious, progressive and full of good people. From the owners and leadership, to the coaching staff, the players and everyone behind the scenes, it’s been a privilege to be part of it.”

Henderson could be joined at Chelsea by Welbeck

Henderson started out at Sunderland before a big-money move to Liverpool in 2011. He made 492 appearances for the Merseyside club, taking over from Steven Gerrard as captain and lifting six major trophies, including the Premier League and Champions League.

A short, ill-advised move to Al-Ettifaq in Saudi Arabia was followed by a spell with Ajax before he joined Brentford.

Henderson’s switch to Chelsea is likely to be completed in the coming days and he could be joined by another thirtysomething in Danny Welbeck.

The Brighton forward is also a target for Chelsea, who are currently on a pre-season tour of Asia.

articles.title: Real Madrid 2026/27: Rodri, Diomande and Cucurella – how the XI could look under Mourinho
articles.summary: Real Madrid are making significant moves in the transfer market and if they can secure their targets, they will have a significantly stronger XI next season
articles.content:
Real Madrid 2026/27: Rodri, Diomande and Cucurella – how the XI could look under Mourinho

Real Madrid are making significant moves in the transfer market and if they can secure their targets, they will have a significantly stronger XI next season

Last Update:

Real Madrid have endured two trophyless seasons with the 2025/26 campaign arguably one of the worst in the club’s illustrious history with dressing room discord undermining the efforts of Xabi Alonso and Alvaro Arbeloa.

Having strengthened his position as president by seeing off the challenge of Enrique Riquelme, Florentino Perez brought Jose Mourinho back to the Santiago Bernabeu and tasked with him with returning the club to glory both domestically and in Europe.

Perez promised to spend big as part of his new mandate but progress so far has been steady rather than spectacular with Marc Cucurella the most lavish investment, the Spain full-back brought in from Chelsea for a fee that could rise to £51.8million.

Denzel Dumfries arrived from Inter Milan for £17.1m while experienced duo Bernardo Silva and Ibrahima Konate joined on free transfers after their contracts expired at Manchester City and Liverpool respectively.

However, that level of prudence is set to end with two big-name players seemingly set to join the Mourinho revolution.

The first will be Yan Diomande, the Ivory Coast winger. Madrid have been locked in talks with RB Leipzig for several weeks and, after a brief stand-off, a resolution appears close.

The 19-year-old is likely to cost Madrid in the region of £102m, making him the most expensive African player of all time. The fee also represents a remarkable piece of business for Leipzig, who signed him from Leganes for £17m just 12 months ago.

Diomande is likely to be joined in the Spanish capital by Rodri. Manchester City’s insistence on keeping the Ballon d’Or and World Cup winner appears to have weakened and talks have reportedly started that would see the 30-year-old return to La Liga after a glorious seven-year spell at the Etihad.

Madrid are not just making progress on players coming in.

Vinicius Jr’s long-standing contract issue is drawing to a conclusion with Madrid’s latest offer likely to be accepted. The Brazilian has less than 12 months left on his current deal, prompting Premier League champions Arsenal to make tentative enquiries, a move that appears to have galvanised Madrid into getting a deal done.

The addition of Diomande and Rodri, as well as keeping Vinicius Jr, would require a huge outlay from Madrid but would provide Mourinho with a new-look line up that would surely get the 15-time European champions back on the right footing.

Here is how they could line-up next season:

Table of Contents

GOALKEEPER

Thibaut CourtoisNo change here with Courtois well-established as one of the best goalkeepers in the world. The giant Belgian is a key cog in the Madrid machine.

DEFENDERS

Right-backDenzel DumfriesThe Netherlands international has been one of the stand-out right-backs in European football over the past few years and his willingness to drive forward and support the attack ought to give Madrid a new dimension.  Right-back was a problem last season with Trent Alexander-Arnold struggling for full fitness and Dani Carvajal falling out of favour. That often led to Federico Valverde playing out of position but that should not happen this term.

Central DefenderIbrahima KonateKonate will probably get the nod over Dean Huijsen due to his physicality. Struggled with off-field issues at Liverpool last season and remains prone to the odd mistake but is set to make up a rugged central pairing with Antonio Rudiger.

Central DefenderAntonio RudigerThe Germany international is now 33 but remains an important member of the Madrid side. Quite similar to Konate in playing style, Rudiger is also an influential voice in the Madrid dressing room. Has been accused of not always using his status wisely but his combative nature is likely to sit well with Mourinho.

Left-backMarc CucurellaThere will be no lack of fight in the Madrid defence next season with Cucurella another who will bring a competitive edge. The outstanding full-back at the World Cup, Cucurella will end Madrid’s problem down the left of their defence.

MIDFIELDERS

RodriThe best in the world in the holding midfield role and arguably the best ever. The Spain international controls the tempo of the game, always looks to play forward and pass through the lines and also comes up with important goals. If Madrid can prise him away from City, it would transform their prospects overnight.

Federico ValverdeEndured a pretty woeful 2025/26 season that saw him shunted between midfield and defence and ended in a training ground fracas with Aurelien Tchouameni that saw him hospitalised. There were bright spots, a brilliant hat-trick against Manchester City in the Champions League, that showed again what he is capable of. The Uruguayan will benefit from some Mourinho love.

Jude BellinghamBellingham is another who struggled to find top gear last season but a brilliant World Cup with England means he should be full of confidence ahead of the new campaign. Technically good, physically strong and good with the ball at his feet – Bellingham possesses every quality required in a modern-day midfielder.

ATTACKERS

Right-wingYan DiomandeYes, Diomande has predominately played on the left but at just 19 years of age, there is no reason why he can’t learn the skills required to play on the opposite side. Quick, strong and deadly in a one-on-one, he will provide great balance to a Madrid attack that has looked lop-sided at times.

Left-wingVinicius JrThe Brazil international often looked disinterested last season and the Bernabeu crowd were quick to let him know they were not impressed. The 26-year-old, who will return to Spain with a new look, will likely use that as fuel to show he is still the star player that has tormented defences over the years. That will be music to Mourinho’s ears.

StrikerKylian MbappeLike Vinicius, Mbappe has endured a love-hate relationship with the Madrid fanbase at times. The ability is unquestionable and his record in Spain of 86 goals across two seasons show he is the perfect man to lead the attack.

articles.title: ‘I made a lot of mistakes’ – Amorim says he learned a lot from Man Utd failings
articles.summary: Former United boss is now with AC Milan
articles.content:
‘I made a lot of mistakes’ – Amorim says he learned a lot from Man Utd failings

Former United boss is now with AC Milan

Last Update:

Former Manchester United manager Ruben Amorim admitted he ‘made a lot of mistakes’ during his tenure at Old Trafford.

The 41-year-old was sacked by United in January after 63 games, winning just 24 with 18 draws and 21 defeats.

Amorim took charge in November 2024 – and was described as the ‘head coach’ by United at the time – but has failed to implement the ideas that made him one of Europe’s most highly regarded tacticians during his time at Sporting CP.

The club finished 15th in the Premier League in his first season, just four points above the relegation zone, with Amorim’s preferred 3-4-3 formation being a regular talking point.

He has now arrived at AC Milan and says he is ready to learn from his errors at the Serie A giants.

“They [Milan] appointed me because they felt I was the right guy for the way I want to play,” Amorim told Sky Italia. “They want to play the same way, but I think they signed me not just for my success, but also for my experience with a top club like Manchester United.

“They understood that I was prepared for this job, not just because of my past success, but also because of my failures. I think it helped a lot in those meetings.”

When asked what went wrong at United, Amorim said: “The first thing is that it doesn’t matter anymore. That is the feeling. There’s a history, then something happens, the context changes, and you focus on the next challenge.

“I learned a lot. It would be hard to point to one thing, but the important thing that I clearly know is that I made a lot of mistakes.

“When you do this kind of reflection, and you understand that it was not just their fault, but also my fault, I think you can be a better coach and a better man.”

Milan finished fifth in Serie A last season and will be in the Europa League.

articles.title: ‘I made history’ – Neymar confirms he has retired from Brazil duty
articles.summary: Neymar retires as Brazil's record goalscorer
articles.content:
‘I made history’ – Neymar confirms he has retired from Brazil duty

Neymar retires as Brazil's record goalscorer

Last Update:

Neymar has retired from international duty with Brazil following their disappointing World Cup.

The 34-year-old is his nation’s record goalscorer with 80 goals in 130 caps and scored in a fourth World Cup with a penalty against Norway.

But he could not save Carlo Ancelotti’s side from an early exit and struggled for fitness throughout.

Back with Santos and back in the headlines, the former Barcelona forward has now confirmed he will not play in the famous yellow shirt again.

“My time with the national team is over. I made history, I was very happy, I gave my all, my life,” he said.

“I always fought and gave my best for this jersey, but I think I don’t want it anymore.”

Neymar made his Brazil debut in 2010, scoring on his debut against the USA. He was a star at the 2014 World Cup until he injured his back and without him Brazil were humiliated 7-1 by Germany in the semi-final.

He won the Confederations Cup in 2013 and was runner-up in the Copa America of 2021 but retires after being unable to guide Brazil to a major honour.

Neymar received criticism in the Brazilian press this week after he took part in a poker tournament while he was returning to full fitness following the World Cup.

The 34-year-old celebrated in his comeback match by pretending to deal poker cards, having explained at the time of the reports that he had trained with Santos and been given permission to pursue his pastime.

Former Al-Hilal, Paris-Saint-Germain and Barcelona playmaker Neymar now has six goals in this season’s Serie A, scoring his first club goals since May 10 on his first Santos appearance since May 17.

articles.title: CONCACAF joins UEFA in condemning FIFA plans for World Cup sell-off
articles.summary: FIFA's plans to create a commercial subsidiary to run major events such as the World Cup has prompted a furious reaction with CONCACAF the latest body to voice its opposition
articles.content:
CONCACAF joins UEFA in condemning FIFA plans for World Cup sell-off

FIFA's plans to create a commercial subsidiary to run major events such as the World Cup has prompted a furious reaction with CONCACAF the latest body to voice its opposition

Last Update:

CONCACAF has become the second confederation to express concern at Gianni Infantino’s plans to sell off parts of FIFA’s major tournaments.

FIFA outlined their intention on Tuesday to create a new commercial subsidiary that would run its main events, including the men’s and women’s World Cup and Club World Cup, and open up investment to external investors.

Football’s world governing body believe it would grow the game by creating greater revenues but critics are concerned it would enable commercial entities to have too great a say over footballing matters as well as increasing the frequency of major tournaments and therefore diluting the quality.

UEFA outlined its opposition yesterday, describing the plans as “crossing a line that football’s governing institutions should never cross,” and CONCACAF followed a similar path on Wednesday.

A statement from the body that oversees Caribbean, North and Central American football said in a statement: “CONCACAF was only made aware of this matter through media reports and, subsequently, via a media release.

“We are deeply concerned by the lack of due process.

“We share the disappointment of many within our region and the game that this level of detail has been designed and shared publicly before any discussion with the relevant governance bodies and stakeholders has taken place.

“As leaders within football, we are the custodians of the game. Collectively, FIFA, the Confederations and every Member Association have a responsibility to always act in the best interests of the sport. Every decision we make must be guided by good governance, robust processes and long-term stewardship.

“This is the framework within which CONCACAF operates. We trust that all within the FIFA family will act in the same manner.”

Table of Contents

US administration consulted over FIFA plan

Under the scheme, FIFA’s 211 member associations would receive a stake that they could either keep or sell to generate income. In addition, it is claimed that Infantino, set to be re-elected unopposed until 2031, would be positioned to become commissioner of the company after his final term as president comes to a close.

A majority stake in the company would be owned by FIFA, with private investors taking on around 20 to 30 per cent and the member nations each possessing a small stake. The plan is reported to have already been discussed among senior FIFA officials and potential stakeholders.

Persons close to the current US presidential administration are reported to have been consulted regarding the scheme and, following initial reports, FIFA confirmed to The Times that the plan is under consideration, with Joshua Kushner — brother of Donald Trump’s son-in-law Jared — the proposed lead investor. American multinational banking firm JP Morgan has also been floated as a potential investor.

The Football Association echoed CONCACAF’s concern about a lack of due process in a statement this morning that read: “We were completely unaware of this proposal and have no substantive details, including what the proposition actually is, and what conditions are attached.

“Based on the limited information, we are deeply concerned about the lack of process and governance to get to this point, and the apparent substance and principles involved.

“When the proposal is shared in the full and transparent way now promised by FIFA, we will make our views clear and comment further.”

UEFA outraged by FIFA plan

UEFA, European football’s governing body, has been hugely critical of Infantino in recent times. It previously accused him of “crossing a red line” in coming to the “incomprehensible and unjustifiable” decision to suspend United States striker Folarin Balogun’s ban for their World Cup last-16 tie with Belgium following apparent pressure from Trump.

And it did not hold back in criticising him again on Tuesday.

A statement from UEFA read: “This crosses a line that football’s governing institutions should never cross. UEFA takes it extremely seriously. So should every National Football Association. So should every stakeholder: leagues, clubs, players, supporters, governments and everyone who cares about the future of the game.

“The soul and governance of football are not assets to trade – especially with zero transparency as to who gains financially. None of us are the owners of football. It is not FIFA’s to sell.”

FIFA plans raise possibility of further World Cup expansion

The idea of giving shares to member associations is viewed as a method of ensuring the plans receive approval from the FIFA congress and council, as for smaller nations the shares would be much more valuable than their annual revenue.

FIFA’s expected revenue for the cycle spanning 2022-26 is anticipated to be $15billion, with much of that stemming from the sale of TV rights for the World Cup as well as funds from sponsorship and ticket and hospitality sales.

After expanding the World Cup from 32 teams to the 48 that contested this year’s tournament, Infantino said this month that a proposal from South America to expand to 64 teams would be looked at. Given the huge amounts of income generated from this year’s competition, private investors would clearly view the World Cup as attractive due to the possibility of expansion or staging the tournament more regularly.

However, one of the biggest winners from the plan coming to fruition would be Infantino. As commissioner or CEO of the new company, he would be expected to command an annual salary akin to that of NFL commissioner Roger Goodell, who earns around $64m a year. Infantino’s current approximate salary is $6m.

articles.title: BREAKING: Real Madrid in talks with Manchester City over signing of Rodri
articles.summary: Real Madrid have targeted Rodri for months and have now opened talks with Manchester City for the Spain midfielder
articles.content:
BREAKING: Real Madrid in talks with Manchester City over signing of Rodri

Real Madrid have targeted Rodri for months and have now opened talks with Manchester City for the Spain midfielder

Last Update:

Real Madrid have made their first move in the pursuit of Rodri by starting talks with Manchester City.

Transfer guru Fabrizio Romano reports that City have finally relented and opened the door to the Spanish club after refusing all previous advances.

Rodri captained Spain to the World Cup title earlier this month and was awarded the Golden Ball as the tournament’s best player.

The 2024 Ballon d’Or winner has flirted with the idea of moving back to his homeland for several months, saying in March: “Having played for Atlético [in 2018-19] before would not prevent me from playing for Real Madrid. There are other players who have done that before. Maybe not direct transfers, but eventually. You can’t turn down one of the world’s best clubs.”

The 30-year-old is currently sidelined after undergoing back surgery but is not expected to be out for long.

Table of Contents

Rodri would bolster Real Madrid midfield

Madrid, now under the returning Jose Mourinho, are looking to bolster their squad after two seasons without a major trophy. One contributing factor has been the lack of experience in midfield following the departures of Toni Kroos and Luka Modric.

Rodri would provide that after proving at the World Cup he was back to his best after struggling to regain top form following a cruciate ligament injury in September 2024.

City have been attempting to persuade him to sign a new deal but the offer has been left on the table for several months and, with less than 12 months to go until his current contract expires, it seems the Etihad club have accepted the player wishes to move on.

His departure would be a major blow to new City boss Enzo Maresca.

What has Maresca said about the situation?

Speaking in his first press conference as City boss last Friday, Maresca expressed calm over the speculation.

“First of all, we have to say that around big players there is always speculation,” Maresca said.

“So I’m not worried about that, it’s normal, also because they [Spain] won the World Cup – he is one of the best players.

“I think every manager wants to have Rodri, because he’s a top player.

“But now, surgery [on a back problem] on Monday, and then he needs holiday, he needs to rest, recovery, and then he will be back here with us.”

articles.title: Vinicius Junior set to stay at Real Madrid amid Arsenal interest
articles.summary: Arsenal transfer target Vinicius Junior will stay at Real Madrid this summer.
articles.content:
Vinicius Junior set to stay at Real Madrid amid Arsenal interest

Arsenal transfer target Vinicius Junior will stay at Real Madrid this summer.

Last Update:

Real Madrid are increasingly confident Vinicius Junior will remain at the Santiago Bernabeu beyond this summer despite ongoing uncertainty surrounding his contract, according to reports.

The Brazil international has been heavily linked with a move away from the Spanish giants, with Premier League champions Arsenal among the clubs credited with an interest.

However, Sky Sports reports that Vinicius is now expected to stay in Madrid, with new head coach Jose Mourinho determined to keep him at the club.

Vinicius has just 11 months remaining on his current deal and, as things stand, would be able to leave on a free transfer in the summer of 2027.

Negotiations over a new contract have yet to produce an agreement, with reports suggesting the 26-year-old wants a salary that would surpass that of Kylian Mbappe, Real Madrid’s highest-paid player.

Vinicius keeping space from training

The Brazilian has reportedly stayed away from first-team training while his future remains unresolved, but Real Madrid have no intention of cashing in during the current transfer window.

According to Sky Sports, the club are confident a new agreement will eventually be reached.

Despite speculation over his future, there has been little indication that Vinicius is actively pushing to leave the Spanish capital.

Vinicius joined Real Madrid from Brazilian side Flamengo in 2018 and has since established himself as one of the club’s most influential players.

He has made more than 375 appearances in all competitions, winning three La Liga titles, two Champions League crowns and two FIFA Club World Cups during his time at the Bernabeu.

articles.title: Cucurella shows off new tattoo after winning World Cup and bids farewell to Chelsea
articles.summary: Marc Cucurella has fulfilled his promise of getting a tattoo of Spain head coach Luis de la Fuente after winning the World Cup.
articles.content:
Cucurella shows off new tattoo after winning World Cup and bids farewell to Chelsea

Marc Cucurella has fulfilled his promise of getting a tattoo of Spain head coach Luis de la Fuente after winning the World Cup.

Last Update:

Marc Cucurella has paid a permanent tribute to Spain manager Luis de la Fuente after helping La Roja win the 2026 World Cup.

Spain claimed their second World Cup title by defeating Argentina in the final, with Ferran Torres scoring the goal to seal victory in North America.

Cucurella, who played a key role, has now honoured his national team boss with a tattoo after fulfilling a promise he made before the competition.

The defender revealed the new ink on Instagram, showing a portrait of De la Fuente holding the World Cup trophy with the tournament’s 2026 logo in the background.

Cucurella had previously vowed to get the tattoo if Spain lifted the trophy, and he documented the entire process before unveiling the finished artwork.

Cucurella says goodbye to Chelsea

The tattoo reveal comes shortly after Cucurella also bid an emotional farewell to Chelsea following his summer move to Real Madrid.

The 28-year-old completed a £51 million transfer to the Spanish giants before the World Cup and is set to reunite with former Chelsea manager Jose Mourinho, who has returned for a second spell in charge at the Santiago Bernabeu.

In a heartfelt message to supporters, Cucurella reflected on his four years at Stamford Bridge and thanked everyone connected with the club.

“I arrived here as a young lad with the dream of winning many trophies and playing in the Champions League,” he wrote.

“We had a tough start, it’s true, but with hard work and effort we were able to turn it around.

“Thanks to this club and its high expectations today, I can honestly say that London will always be my home and you will always be part of my story.

“I won’t forget listening to my song at the stadium, the magical nights at the Bridge, the titles that I’ve won carrying this badge and all the love that you showed me.

“I now leave the club being a man. I’ve reached a lot of my dreams thanks to you and I want to thank you all for that.

“To the coaches and staff for all the advice that you gave me, to my teammates, for all that we have lived together and I won’t forget.

“To all the people working at Cobham for making me feel like I was at home from day one. I truly hope to see Chelsea up where they belong and deserve to be. Once a Blue, always a Blue.”

articles.title: Alonso sees ‘value’ in Chelsea’s 10-goal pre-season thriller
articles.summary: Xabi Alonso has spoken after Chelsea' 6-4 win over Sydney Wanderers in pre-season.
articles.content:
Alonso sees ‘value’ in Chelsea’s 10-goal pre-season thriller

Xabi Alonso has spoken after Chelsea' 6-4 win over Sydney Wanderers in pre-season.

Last Update:

Chelsea head coach Xabi Alonso believes his side’s entertaining 6-4 pre-season win over Western Sydney Wanderers will prove valuable as they continue to prepare for the new campaign.

The Blues made a winning start to their Sydney Super Cup campaign in Alonso’s first match in charge, although the Spaniard admitted there were periods where his team struggled to cope with their opponents’ pressing.

Dastan Satpayev gave Chelsea an early lead before the Wanderers hit back with two goals. Dario Essugo restored parity before half-time, while Jamie Gittens and a nine-minute hat-trick from Joao Pedro helped Chelsea pull away after the break.

Despite the victory, Alonso felt the match highlighted areas his side must improve.

“I think this friendly is going to be very useful for the future,” Alonso said.

“There were moments in the game where we were struggling to find solutions, and we needed to experience that.

“The positive is that we corrected them, but these moments of game management are something we can learn from.

“When they were pressing so high, it was difficult to find solutions through the middle. We need a better understanding of what is happening and be able to make changes during the game because it’s something we’ll face often.

“The more situations we experience where we struggle and then find solutions, the better team we will become.”

Alonso hails academy talent

Alonso also highlighted the positives from the opening fixture of Chelsea’s tour, with several academy players featuring alongside established first-team stars.

“There were no injuries, the young players gained valuable experience by coming on tour and playing minutes, and the senior players made a good impact when they came on,” he added.

“It was an exciting game for the fans as well.”

Romeo Lavia was the only senior player in the matchday squad not to feature, with Alonso revealing the midfielder was left out as a precaution after feeling discomfort in his hamstring.

“He felt something in his hamstring,” Alonso explained.

“It’s nothing serious and we’re hopeful he’ll be fit for Saturday against Tottenham. There was no point taking any risks today, which is why Reggie Watson played the full 90 minutes and did well.”

articles.title: ‘Football is not FIFA’s to sell – UEFA slams Infantino over plans to sell stakes in World Cup
articles.summary: The scheme could see the FIFA president earn a $64m annual salary.
articles.content:
‘Football is not FIFA’s to sell – UEFA slams Infantino over plans to sell stakes in World Cup

The scheme could see the FIFA president earn a $64m annual salary.

Last Update:

UEFA accused FIFA president Gianni Infantino of “crossing a line that football’s governing institutions should never cross” it emerged that he is drawing up plans to sell stakes in the World Cup sold to private investors.

An initial report by the Times revealed that the scheme would see a company put together to oversee FIFA’s top competitions in the men’s and women’s games, including the World Cup and the Club World Cup. The plan could see Infantino earn tens of millions and raise the possibility of the World Cup and Club World Cup being held more often than every four years.

Under the scheme, FIFA’s 211 member associations would receive a stake that they could either keep or sell to generate income. In addition, it is claimed that Infantino, set to be re-elected unopposed until 2031, would be positioned to become commissioner of the company after his final term as president comes to a close.

A majority stake in the company would be owned by FIFA, with private investors taking on around 20 to 30 per cent and the member nations each possessing a small stake. The plan is reported to have already been discussed among senior FIFA officials and potential stakeholders.

Persons close to the current US presidential administration are reported to have been consulted regarding the scheme and, following initial reports, FIFA confirmed to The Times that the plan is under consideration, with Joshua Kushner — brother of Donald Trump’s son-in-law Jared — the proposed lead investor. American multinational banking firm JP Morgan has also been floated as a potential investor.

Table of Contents

UEFA slams Infantino plans

UEFA, European football’s governing body, has been hugely critical of Infantino in recent times. It previously accused him of “crossing a red line” in coming to the  “incomprehensible and unjustifiable” to suspend United States striker Folarin Balogun’s ban for their World Cup last-16 tie with Belgium following apparent pressure from US president Donald Trump.

And it did not hold back in criticising him again on Tuesday.

A statement from UEFA read: “This crosses a line that football’s governing institutions should never cross. UEFA takes it extremely seriously. So should every National Football Association. So should every stakeholder: leagues, clubs, players, supporters, governments and everyone who cares about the future of the game.

“The soul and governance of football are not assets to trade – especially with zero transparency as to who gains financially. None of us are the owners of football. It is not FIFA’s to sell.”

In a later statement confirming the plans: “In accordance with its mandate, the FIFA administration is exploring the concept of bringing together FIFA’s commercial rights – spanning broadcast, sponsorship, ticketing, and licensing – with the operational delivery of FIFA tournaments through the creation of FIFA Forward Enterprise (FFE). A consultation process has begun following the receipt of a proposal that aims to unlock the full potential of FIFA’s broadcast rights and sponsorships across all of its tournament portfolio in men’s, women’s and youth football.

Central to this would be a repositioning of FIFA Forward, FIFA’s flagship development programme, which aims to increase funding per FIFA Member Association (MA) from USD 8 million to USD 20 million for the 2027-30 cycle and grow steadily thereafter cycle-on-cycle. This funding would support infrastructure, coaching, national teams, competitions, grassroots football and the women’s game.

The process follows an address by FIFA President Gianni Infantino to the FIFA Council and FIFA Member Associations on the eve of the FIFA World Cup 2026 final in New York, where he reiterated his intention to “unleash the commercial potential and opportunity that FIFA has”, a position that had already been outlined in his speech to the FIFA Congress in Vancouver, Canada, in April 2026.

Infantino said: “Football is the world’s most popular sport and an extraordinary engine of human and social development. Parts of the game have turned that popularity into remarkable commercial value – and we celebrate that success and want it to continue, because it lifts the whole game. Our job is to make sure the rest of football grows with it: FIFA exists to support sustainable, inclusive development in every corner of the world.

“As its global governing body, FIFA is responsible for making sure the game reaches every corner of the world, and that the value it creates supports federations and communities everywhere. Our next stage of growth needs a structure built for it, one where the commercial side of the game operates as a focused, dedicated business, with its value shared more and better all around the world. Every FIFA Member Association should have an opportunity to seek a fair share of the available funding to shape its own future, deciding for itself rather than relying on others. This is about the democratisation of football worldwide.

“We intend to invest heavily even in the smallest or most remote parts of the footballing world, places that are too often passed over. Every FIFA Member Association, whatever its size, resources, or geographic location will have a voice and the opportunity to determine its own course. Football has become a truly global game and so the benefits must be felt globally.”

The statement continued: “In a similar way to other sports governing bodies with dedicated commercial subsidiaries, FIFA will invite third parties to make minority, non-controlling investments in FFE.

“Any such investors would be selected against clear long-term, governance, and strategic criteria. They would represent a geographically diversified group that reflects the global nature of the game, acting as minority, long-term partners that could contribute capital and commercial expertise in support of FIFA’s mission to grow the global game. FIFA would retain sole control of FFE via majority board representation and exclusive authority over football governance, competitions, the international match calendar and all regulatory and sporting decisions.

“While FIFA regularly creates subsidiaries for specific ventures unilaterally, FIFA is now engaging the MAs and the FIFA Council in this instance given its strategic importance. In keeping with the democratic processes of FIFA, the FIFA administration will launch the new structure only if a majority of the MAs decide to support it, as well as approval of the required regulatory updates by the FIFA Council.

“Subject to these final agreements and required approvals, Thrive Eternal, a permanent capital holding company, is expected to lead the proposed investor group for FFE. Greg Maffei, CEO of BANN Ventures and formerly President and CEO of Liberty Media during its acquisition and ownership of Formula One, has been a key commercial adviser and will remain involved in the establishment of FFE in this next phase.

“As part of this process, J.P. Morgan has been engaged to work alongside FIFA, while other advisers such as OpenEconomics are engaging with prospective long-term investors. The process is focused on assembling a geographically diversified investor group that reflects the global nature of FIFA and the game; expressions of interest to date include investors from across every major region of the world: Europe, the Americas, Asia and Africa.

“The FIFA President and the FIFA administration have a duty to control the development of this project. Outside investors will have only a minority stake in FFE and will not play any operational role. Equally, they are investing in a subsidiary of FIFA, and not in FIFA itself. For FIFA, nothing changes.”

Plans raise possibility of further World Cup expansion

The idea of giving shares to member associations is viewed as a method of ensuring the plans receive approval from the FIFA congress and council, as for smaller nations the shares would be much more valuable than their annual revenue.

FIFA’s expected revenue for the cycle spanning 2022-26 is anticipated to be $15billion, with much of that stemming from the sale of TV rights for the World Cup as well as funds from sponsorship and ticket and hospitality sales.

After expanding the World Cup from 32 teams to the 48 that contested this year’s tournament, Infantino said this month that a proposal from South America to expand to 64 teams would be looked at. Given the huge amounts of income generated from this year’s competition, private investors would clearly view the World Cup as attractive due to the possibility of expansion or staging the tournament more regularly.

However, one of the biggest winners from the plan coming to fruition would be Infantino. As commissioner or CEO of the new company, he would be expected to command an annual salary akin to that of NFL commissioner Roger Goodell, who earns around $64m a year. Infantino’s current approximate salary is $6m.

articles.title: No letter, no fax and no call – Bayern Munich chief says Real Madrid have not been in touch over Michael Olise
articles.summary: Michael Olise has enjoyed a wonderful two years at Bayern Munich and he is set to remain in the Bundesliga
articles.content:
No letter, no fax and no call – Bayern Munich chief says Real Madrid have not been in touch over Michael Olise

Michael Olise has enjoyed a wonderful two years at Bayern Munich and he is set to remain in the Bundesliga

Last Update:

Bayern Munich CEO Jan-Christian Dreesen insists the club have not received a single offer from Real Madrid for Michael Olise this summer and says the Bundesliga champions have no intention of selling the France international.

Olise joined Bayern from Crystal Palace in 2024 and has made a huge impact, winning the Bundesliga in each of his two seasons in Germany as well as the club’s player of the season award in 2025 and 2026.

The 24-year-old, who was born in London but declared for France having come through Les Bleus’ youth system, made a brilliant start at the World Cup as Didier Deschamps’ men cruised through the group stage but then faded as they exited in the semi-finals to eventual winners Spain.

Olise’s form for club and country caught the eye of Madrid, who were reported to be readying a £200m bid for the former Reading midfielder this summer. But Dreesen says no approach has been made by the Liga giants and one would not be welcomed.

Asked if Olise would stay at Bayern, he told Kicker: “Yes, of course. We have received no letter, no fax and no call from Real Madrid. It’s astonishing what [rumours] can end up being spread when you know yourself what the truth actually is.”

Bayern don’t want to sell Olise, or Luis Díaz

Dreesen also suggested £200m would not be enough even if Madrid were to get in touch.

He added: “I have not heard a single one [person in my circle of friends] who said that at £200m you have to sell him. He still has three years left on his contract.”

Another Bayern star linked with a move away from the Allianz Arena is Colombia winger Luis Diaz.

Diaz is a rumoured target for Saudi side Al-Hilal but Dreesen adopted a similar stance.

He said: “We’d be stupid if we sell Diaz, wouldn’t we? We have such a fantastic squad, honestly. Let’s just get the season underway and start scoring some goals.”

Diaz made a strong impression in his first year at Bayern, scoring 26 goals in 51 games in all competitions.

articles.title: Mancini set for Italy return after Pirlo deal collapse
articles.summary: Mancini will take over after an agreement with Andrea Pirlo fell apart.
articles.content:
Mancini set for Italy return after Pirlo deal collapse

Mancini will take over after an agreement with Andrea Pirlo fell apart.

Last Update:

Roberto Mancini is set to return for a second spell as Italy coach, according to multiple reports, with Claudio Ranieri also poised to join the national team set-up.

Having been turned down by Pep Guardiola and Carlo Ancelotti, the Italian Football Federation (FIGC) was poised to appoint former Azzurri midfielder Andrea Pirlo.

However, the deal for him to take over fell apart due to his association with a Russian sports betting platform, which led to significant political pressure on FIGC president Giovanni Malago to block his appointment.

Pirlo confirmed in a statement that he was informed on Sunday that he was no longer in the running for the job.

The 2006 World Cup winner is under contract with Dubai club United FC while also serving as a global brand ambassador for Russian betting provider Fonbet.

He stressed that the collaboration was “exclusively commercial and sporting in nature” – but after reviewing the contract documents, the FIGC leadership and Malago reached a different conclusion.

That led to Paolo Maldini stepping down as FIGC technical director just 16 days into his role.

Now, as the FIGC seeks to draw a line under the farce, it has looked to Mancini to lead the task of turning around the Azzurri’s fortunes following their latest World Cup failure.

Meanwhile Ranieri is said to be set to replace Maldini as technical director. Ranieri turned down the chance to become coach last June before Italy appointed Gennaro Gattuso. The 74-year-old’s last job in football was as a special advisor to Roma, a position he left in April, and he will assume a key position in the FIGC hierarchy with a coaching career that took him to 20 different stops seemingly at an end.

Mancini, who left his role as coach of Qatari side Al-Sadd earlier this year, led Italy to glory at Euro 2020 before a five-year spell in charge came to an end in 2023.

He inherits a team that came agonisingly close to ending Italy’s World Cup absence, with a penalty shootout defeat to Bosnia-Herzegovina in their UEFA qualifying play-off final denying them a spot in the finals in North America.

Having missed out on two World Cups and exited Euro 2024 in the last 16 following their Wembley penalty shootout defeat of England, Italy have not won a knockout game at a major tournament since Mancini guided them to a second European Championship title in 2021.

Mancini does not have an easy start to his bid to turn things around, as his first game will come against Belgium in the UEFA Nations League on September 25 before the Azzurri then face Turkey and France in the same competition in an extended international break.

articles.title: BREAKING: Josko Gvardiol signs new five-year contract with Manchester City
articles.summary: Josko Gvardiol has committed his future to Manchester City
articles.content:
BREAKING: Josko Gvardiol signs new five-year contract with Manchester City

Josko Gvardiol has committed his future to Manchester City

Last Update:

Josko Gvardiol has signed a new contract at Manchester City that ties him to the club until 2031.

The Croatia international, who can operate at left-back or centre-half, joined City from RB Leipzig in 2023 and has made 122 appearances in all competitions, helping the club claim the Premier League title as well as the FA Cup and EFL Cup.

The 24-year-old told the club’s official website: “As soon as I knew City wanted to renew my contract, I felt straight away it was what I wanted.

“The City fans have been unbelievable with me from day one – and the club provide absolutely everything for players. It’s the best club in the world to be at.

“I have felt so much love and respect during my three years here and I don’t take that for granted.

“The players we have here are amazing. This is a world-class squad that is young and full of potential. I truly believe we will have a lot of success in the coming years.”

Injuries disrupted Gvardiol’s progress at City last season

Gvardiol suffered a broken shinbone against Chelsea in January that saw him miss the bulk of the second half of last season but he recovered in time to play for Croatia at the World Cup.

And director of football Hugo Viana is excited at what the former Dinamo Zagreb man will produce over the coming years under new boss Enzo Maresca.

Viana said: “Josko is a player this club really believes in. He is young, an outstanding professional and already one of the best defenders in the world.

“Manchester City are committed to keeping our best talent, which is why we are so happy this new contract has been agreed.

“Josko epitomises what we want in our defenders – he can play multiple positions, is quick, strong and when he attacks he does it superbly. He is exceptional.

“But the way he conducts himself is also very impressive. This is a young man determined to be the best he can be – an approach that is totally aligned with our overall vision.

“I want to congratulate Josko on this new deal and everyone at City is now focused on ensuring he maximises his potential.”

Gvardiol will be a key figure for Maresca with City losing John Stones and Nathan Ake over the summer.

articles.title: Manchester City provide Rodri injury update amid continued Real Madrid speculation
articles.summary: Rodri continues to be linked with a return to his homeland.
articles.content:
Manchester City provide Rodri injury update amid continued Real Madrid speculation

Rodri continues to be linked with a return to his homeland.

Last Update:

Manchester City have confirmed Rodri has undergone successful back surgery.

Rodri won the Golden Ball at the World Cup as he helped Spain lift the trophy for the second time, but returned with an issue that required a minor operation.

A statement from City read in part: “The midfielder had been feeling discomfort for some time but has now undergone a procedure to address the issue and will now begin a short period of rehabilitation.”

The update from City comes as Rodri continues to be linked with a move back to his homeland to join Real Madrid.

Table of Contents

Doubts over Rodri’s future

Rodri’s contract at the Etihad Stadium expires at the end of the coming season.

A contract offer from City has reportedly been on the table for some time and, while he is yet to accept, there is said to be internal optimism a deal will be done.

However, interest from Madrid could ruin City’s plans to keep the 2024 Ballon d’Or winner at the club.

Having previously indicated they were not interested in signing the 30-year-old, Madrid appear to have changed that stance and City are now braced for a bid from Los Blancos.

What has Maresca said about the situation?

Speaking in his first press conference as City boss last Friday, Enzo Maresca expressed calm over the speculation surrounding Rodri.

“First of all, we have to say that around big players there is always speculation,” Maresca said.

“So I’m not worried about that, it’s normal, also because they [Spain] won the World Cup – he is one of the best players.

“I think every manager wants to have Rodri, because he’s a top player.

“But now, surgery [on a back problem] on Monday, and then he needs holiday, he needs to rest, recovery, and then he will be back here with us.”

articles.title: Former Real Madrid goalkeeper accuses club of ‘unforgivable mismanagement’ over Vinicius Jr contract saga
articles.summary: Vinicius Jr could leave Real Madrid this summer and the club's former goalkeeper Santiago Canizares is not impressed
articles.content:
Former Real Madrid goalkeeper accuses club of ‘unforgivable mismanagement’ over Vinicius Jr contract saga

Vinicius Jr could leave Real Madrid this summer and the club's former goalkeeper Santiago Canizares is not impressed

Last Update:

Former Real Madrid goalkeeper Santiago Canizares has accused the club of “unforgivable mismanagement” over Vinicius Jr’s new contract.

The Brazil winger has less than 12 months left on his current deal and Arsenal are believed to have sounded out his representatives over a move to the Emirates this summer.

Madrid’s pursuit of RB Leipzig’s Ivorian winger Yan Diomande, who plays in Vinicius Jr’s preferred left-wing position, has added further fuel to the fire that the 26-year-old could have played his last game for the club.

And Canizares, who made 41 appearances for Madrid before a hugely successful spell with Valencia and Spain, believes the current lack of discourse around a new deal for the two-time Champions League winner is not a good sign.

He told Cadena COPE: “The more noise there is on a player, the less likely he is to leave.

“Real Madrid are late on everything. If it is true that he does not have a signed agreement, Real Madrid has the obligation to sell him.

“You can’t lose 100 or one hundred and something million euros for letting a player finish his contract. I just think it’s going to happen. It’s unforgivable mismanagement.”

Madrid maintain Diomande pursuit

Madrid are desperate to keep Vinicius Jr, who has recently undergone chin reconstruction, and pair him with Diomande, who returned to training with Leipzig yesterday.

Sky Germany claim an initial £85million bid has been rejected by Leipzig but a fresh offer of £98m has seen talks resume. It is thought that if Madrid increase that to around £102m then Diomande would become a Real Madrid player.

That would represent a remarkable return for Leipzig who bought the winger from Leganes 12 months ago having met his release clause of £17m.

If he does move to the Santiago Bernabeu, Diomande would become the most expensive African player in history, surpassing the £72m Arsenal paid for Nicolas Pepe in 2019.

The 19-year-old made four appearances in the United States, Canada and Mexico but largely underwhelmed as the Ivorians lost to Norway at the round of 32 stage.

articles.title: BREAKING: Zinedine Zidane confirmed as new France boss
articles.summary: Zinedine Zidane will replace Didier Deschamps as France boss
articles.content:
BREAKING: Zinedine Zidane confirmed as new France boss

Zinedine Zidane will replace Didier Deschamps as France boss

Last Update:

Zinedine Zidane has been named the new head coach of France, replacing Didier Deschamps.

Deschamps left the role following Les Bleus’ run to the World Cup semi-finals, where they lost to eventual winners Spain before also losing the third/fourth place play-off to England.

It ended 14 years in charge for Deschamps, who led France to World Cup glory in 2018 and the final four years later in Qatar.

France legend and 1998 Ballon d’Or winner Zidane has not managed since the second of his two spells with Real Madrid ended after 26 months in charge in 2021.

Having won the 2001/02 Champions League and 2002/03 Liga title as a player with the Spanish giants, Zidane won the Spanish title and became a European champion in three consecutive seasons during his first spell as their manager, between 2016 and 2018.

He has signed a four-year contract to guide France through the 2030 World Cup.

Table of Contents

Zidane is one of the legends of football in France – FFF chief Diallo

Philippe Diallo, the president of the French Football Federation (FFF), said: “It is an incredible moment that we are living this morning. It has been almost 14 years since the FFF had been confronted with the situation of choosing a new coach.

“In February 2025, I met Zinédine Zidane. I contacted him to offer him a mission at the head of our French team. Since then, we have met several times to discuss his arrival. It was the meeting of two desires. A desire because Zinédine is one of the legends of French football and he had made it known that one of his dreams was to lead the French team. On the part of the Federation, a desire to have someone who has the aura, the competence and the heart of our fans to lead one of the best teams in the world.

“I have the privilege, the great honour and also the emotion to tell you that Zidane will be the next coach of the French team for the next four years, which will cover the qualifications for the Nations League, Euro 2028 and the 2030 World Cup. This contract will take effect on August 1. He will present his staff in early September.”

Zidane reveals he rejected offers to return to management

Zidane, who made 108 appearances for France, scoring 31 goals, including two in the 1998 World Cup final win over Brazil, admitted he had been waiting for this opportunity for sometime.

He said: “It’s a dream. I had proposals during the past four or five years to take over a club. And I refused them all for the French team, because it was the only thing I wanted to do after my experience at Real Madrid. The only thing that drives me is to be able to work for this team and that it continues to win.

“It’s an immense joy. I am happy with what is happening to me today. I am calm but I have a lot of emotions in me. I’m ready for the challenge, that’s what drives me.”

Turkey test first up for France and Zidane

Zidane’s first games in charge will be in the Nations League in the four-game international window across September and October.

September 25: Turkey v France

September 28: Belgium v France

October 2: France v Italy

October 5: France v Belgium

“I have an extraordinary team,” said Zidane. “I will explain my game project to them.

“I have always looked at this team as a supporter, but also as a coach. That’s why I didn’t take a club. From the day after Deschamps’ decision in early 2025, I was animated by this desire to be next. The agreement was sealed as soon as I met the president.

“My priority is the first match against Turkey. I will have three weeks with the players in September, it’s great, almost unprecedented to be able to prepare things with them.

“There is no trap, it is a completely different job than that at a club. It doesn’t scare me. As this is what I wanted to do, I will have a balance between my personal life and the French team, it suits me perfectly. It’s a different job, I have no difficulties with that.”
