articles.title: Former Real Madrid captain Nacho believes Jose Mourinho will inspire Bernabeu bounce back: ‘Beautiful things are coming’
articles.summary: Nacho has lifted the Champions League trophy with Real Madrid and he is confident the good times will return under Jose Mourinho
articles.content:
Former Real Madrid captain Nacho believes Jose Mourinho will inspire Bernabeu bounce back: ‘Beautiful things are coming’

Nacho has lifted the Champions League trophy with Real Madrid and he is confident the good times will return under Jose Mourinho

Last Update:

Former Real Madrid captain Nacho believes “beautiful things are coming” under Jose Mourinho.

Madrid have not won a major trophy for two seasons and suffered a miserable 2025/26 campaign that started with high hopes under Xabi Alonso but ended in acrimony and in-fighting with Alvaro Arbeloa at the helm.

Mourinho was brought back to restore the good times and also bring harmony to a fractured dressing room. And Nacho, who captained the club to their 15th Champions League title in 2024 under Carlo Ancelotti, is confident the Portuguese will get the players onside and inspire an uptick in fortunes.

In an interview with AS, the Al Qadsiah defender said: “What I am clear about – and I don’t know if in the end titles will be won because this is football and it is not easy – he will have the players motivated, he will have them 100%.

“The intensity that he puts into every training session and every game, I have seen, I can assure you that they are 100%. So, if the players and Mourinho manage to all be together, I have no doubt that good things will come for Real Madrid.

“Mou is from Real Madrid, he is a Madrid man. That’s the important thing, he knows perfectly what it is to win and what it is to lose at this club. If the players are with him to the death, beautiful things are coming for Real Madrid.”

Table of Contents

New Real Madrid boss Mourinho is a ‘special person’

Nacho worked with Mourinho during his first spell at the Santiago Bernabeu and made his debut under the former Chelsea and Manchester United boss in a chaotic 6-3 win at Valencia in 2011.

“Mourinho is a special person for me and my family,” added Nacho, 36. “He is a coach who marked my career, the one who gave me the opportunity. As a result of that match in Mestalla, many more matches came with the first team. Mou will always be special to me. Regardless of whether he is a great coach, and he is for me and for my whole family, he is THE coach, so to speak.

“I remember that stage as one of the best of my life.”

Nacho backs Cucurella to succeed at Real Madrid

One of Mourinho’s first signings this summer was that of Spain full-back Marc Cucurella, who had a brilliant World Cup as La Roja lifted the crown.

Nacho believes the Catalonian’s fighting spirit will benefit the capital club.

“He is intense, always wanting to fight for his team,” he said. “He brings together the perfect characteristics to play for Real Madrid. Also, he is a player that is needed right now, in which this intensity is required.”

articles.title: English football to trial new method of preventing goalkeeper time wasting
articles.summary: The Premier League is set for a rule change ahead of the 2026/27 campaign.
articles.content:
English football to trial new method of preventing goalkeeper time wasting

The Premier League is set for a rule change ahead of the 2026/27 campaign.

Last Update:

English football will introduce a new trial this season aimed at stamping out the increasingly common tactic of goalkeepers stopping play to allow coaches to deliver team talks.

The Football Association, Premier League, English Football League, National League and Women’s Super League have all agreed to the measure after receiving approval from the International Football Association Board (IFAB).

Under the new trial, if a referee signals for the physio to treat a goalkeeper, the goalkeeper’s team must remove an outfield player from the pitch for one minute once play resumes.

The coach will have 10 seconds to nominate which player leaves the field by informing the fourth official. If no player is selected within that time, the team captain will automatically be required to leave the pitch.

The first match to use the new rule will be Saturday’s Carabao Cup preliminary-round tie between Tranmere Rovers and Rochdale.

Australia’s A-League is also set to trial a variation of the law, although there the captain will always be the player required to leave the field.

The move comes after growing frustration over goalkeepers appearing to go down injured simply to halt the game, allowing team-mates to gather around the technical area for tactical instructions or disrupting the opposition’s momentum.

Last season, Leeds United manager Daniel Farke accused Manchester City goalkeeper Gianluigi Donnarumma of “bending the rules” by feigning injury to break up play.

English football believes forcing a team to play with 10 men for a minute will provide a far stronger deterrent than simply preventing players from approaching the touchline.

The trial mirrors the current law for outfield players, who must leave the pitch for one minute if they receive treatment from the physio.

There are several exceptions where an outfield player will not have to leave the field:

If the goalkeeper is substituted, the change can be made immediately without delay.

IFAB will monitor the results of the trial throughout the season before deciding whether to introduce the law permanently worldwide from the 2027-28 campaign.

John Stones set to join Inter Milan as free agent

John Stones is set to become an Inter Milan player this summer.

England defender John Stones is in advanced talks with Inter Milan over a move to the Serie A champions following his departure from Manchester City.

The 32-year-old is available on a free transfer after his contract at the Etihad expired at the end of June.

Stones attracted interest from several leading European clubs, including Chelsea and Juventus, but Inter are now understood to be leading the race for his signature after positive discussions over a proposed two-year contract.

On the international stage, Stones has earned 93 caps for England and was part of the Three Lions squad that secured a third-place finish at the 2026 World Cup.

articles.title: Italy head coach hunt descends into chaos after Pirlo ruled out as Maldini resigns
articles.summary: The hunt for Italy's new head coach has descended into chaos.
articles.content:
Italy head coach hunt descends into chaos after Pirlo ruled out as Maldini resigns

The hunt for Italy's new head coach has descended into chaos.

Last Update:

Italy failed to qualify for the 2026 World Cup. They then watched it from home as the rest of the world played on.

And now, as they attempt to rebuild, the process has collapsed into exactly the kind of embarrassing farce that explains how they ended up in this mess in the first place.

Andrea Pirlo has been ruled out of the Italy head coach position due to his association with a Russian sports betting platform, which led to significant political pressure on FIGC president Giovanni Malago to block his appointment.

Pirlo confirmed in a statement that he was informed late on Sunday night that he was no longer in the running for the job.

Pirlo is currently under contract with Dubai club United FC while also serving as a global brand ambassador for Russian betting provider Fonbet.

He stressed that the collaboration was “exclusively commercial and sporting in nature” – but after reviewing the contract documents, the federation leadership around Malago reached a different conclusion.

The federal lawyer spent the weekend examining the contract and found it was not directly tied to his role as manager of United FC, which is owned by Sergey Lomakin, but was rather a personal partnership.

FIGC’s priority candidate was Pep Guardiola, who rejected the opportunity. Carlo Ancelotti also turned it down.

That left Pirlo as the option backed by technical director Paolo Maldini – himself only appointed a fortnight ago – and his advisor Leonardo.

Malago’s own preferred candidate had been Roberto Mancini, who had resigned from Al-Sadd in June and was ready for a second stint in charge. Mancini is reported to feel “abandoned” by the federation and is furious that he was passed over.

Malago picking up the pieces

Now Malago is left picking up the pieces.

“The new coach? I’ve been receiving tons of messages since this morning,” the FIGC president said.

“I’ll speak to everyone as soon as possible, as is only right.” He added: “He’ll be here soon, by tomorrow. I’m working on it.”

When pressed on whether Thiago Motta was a candidate, his response was: “I can’t say yes or no. Who was I referring to when I spoke of embarrassing situations? Everyone is free to interpret it as they wish.”

The fallout has extended to Maldini, who has now resigned as technical director, alongside Leonardo.

Even Italian politics has been dragged in. Deputy Prime Minister Matteo Salvini, speaking at the presentation of Roma’s new stadium plans, was asked about the situation.

Malago insists the bigger picture is clear even if the immediate next step is not. “To recover our competitive credibility at the top level, where nothing is guaranteed, you need to work on kids who are now between 13 and 16 years old,” he said.

“For this, you need to change the entire process in terms of training and culture, and this also includes the coach. The ideas are very clear.”

articles.title: Why Danny Welbeck could be crucial signing for Chelsea
articles.summary: Danny Welbeck could become Chelsea's only player aged over 28
articles.content:
Why Danny Welbeck could be crucial signing for Chelsea

Danny Welbeck could become Chelsea's only player aged over 28

Last Update:

Perhaps the greatest surprise about Chelsea’s pursuit of Brighton & Hove Albion’s Danny Welbeck is the level-headed judgement the move suggests from a club not always renowned for clever recruitment.

Welbeck turns 36 in November but his form suggests he is at his peak after the best season of his impressive career in 2025/26, with his tally of 13 goals and total of 2,265 minutes representing his best figures in a Premier League campaign.

Before joining Brighton on an initial one-year deal after his Watford contract was terminated in 2020, Welbeck had not scored more than five goals in a league season since he netted nine times for Manchester United in 2013/14.

Having hit double figures in each of the last two seasons, Welbeck can add to Chelsea’s firepower – but the variety of his game and influence off the pitch may appeal most to new head coach Xabi Alonso.

Table of Contents

Danny Welbeck: Why Chelsea want transfer deal

Chelsea have had Brighton’s executives on speed dial over recent years, paying a then British-transfer record £115m for Moises Caicedo, £55m for Joao Pedro, an initial £47.5m for Marc Cucurella, £25m for goalkeeper Robert Sanchez and millions more in compensation for former head coach Graham Potter and his staff in 2022.

They are likely to find the Seagulls hard bargainers again for Welbeck, who is in the final year of his contract but has become crucial to Albion’s fortunes under head coach Fabian Hurzeler.

Only three English players bettered Welbeck’s total of 13 league goals in 2025/26 and it is unlikely many had more of a positive effect in the dressing room at their clubs.

With Hurzeler in his first Premier League role and the youngest manager in the top flight at 33, the former St Pauli boss has counted on Welbeck to be a role model, winning the Players’ Player of the Season award in May.

Hurzeler and Welbeck’s teammates have effusively praised his inspirational presence, which will appeal to Alonso after his experience in charge of a Real Madrid squad whose attitude was often questioned during the Spaniard’s brief time in charge at the start of last season.

Chelsea are not short of attacking options, making Welbeck’s exemplary attitude and proven willingness to be a steadying squad member rather than a superstar important.

Brighton have brought Welbeck on 52 times and substituted him off 80 times during his time at the club, with Hurzeler urging his players to emulate Welbeck’s tireless defensive work after a win over Newcastle last season.

“I will clip all the sprints back and, all the time, how Danny defends,” Hurzeler told his squad in an address caught on camera in the post-match dressing room.

“He gets the rewards for how he works defensively. That’s the main thing and that’s the benchmark.”

Danny Welbeck age: Is he too old for Chelsea?

Alonso’s reported interest in 33-year-old Sunderland captain Granit Xhaka – Black Cats boss Regis Le Bris says the midfielder will not be leaving – indicates the type of experience and intelligence he wants to add to his squad.

Alongside 18 years in senior club football, Welbeck has been unfortunate not to increase his total of 42 England caps under current Three Lions boss Thomas Tuchel, who was tipped by many to give Welbeck the chance to add to his 16 international goals.

Welbeck’s proneness to injury cannot be attributed primarily to age and has improved significantly during his mid-30s.

He first suffered serious knee problems with United in 2009/10, followed by more in 2014/15 with Arsenal, sitting out much of 2015/16 and 2016/17.

An ankle injury kept him out for almost all of the 2018/19 season and he missed more than three months for Watford in 2019/20 because of a hamstring injury.

With Brighton, Welbeck missed 14 games because of a hamstring issue in 2021/22 and 11 in 2023/24.

That track record shows how Welbeck requires careful physical management, which Albion appear to have successfully achieved.

Their talisman made 49 league appearances across his first two seasons, averaged 30 over the subsequent three and played in all but one game in 2025/26.

Danny Welbeck goals: Striker haunts Chelsea

Several of Welbeck’s more memorable Albion goals have come against Chelsea, who are the side he has scored most against in the Premier League.

Welbeck will have work to do to match his existing tally of five goals at Stamford Bridge, as well as netting twice against them in home matches.

Clinical Welbeck finds different ways to score stylishly: by the time he reached his half-century for Brighton last season, Albion Analytics put Welbeck’s figures for the club at 12 match-winning goals, registering through 13 headers, 11 goals with his left foot and 26 with his right.

Should he leave Brighton, Welbeck’s last goal for the Seagulls will have come against Chelsea at the Amex Stadium during a 3-0 win over Chelsea on April 21.

The thrashing spelled the end of Liam Rosenior’s fleeting time as Chelsea manager, although the Premier League rookie had time to lambast his squad’s sulky performance in the immediate aftermath.

When Hurzeler came under pressure in February after a dismal mid-season run, Welbeck’s performances and standard-bearing behind the scenes were among the key reasons why Brighton turned their form around in stirring fashion to qualify for Europe.

Had Rosenior had more characters of Welbeck’s class to call upon, he may have found his time at Chelsea considerably less challenging.

Danny Welbeck stats

Welbeck has more than a goal every four matches for Brighton – and that average has gone up from one in five in 2023/24 to one in three the following season and more than one in three in 2025/26.

Accuracy is a hallmark of Welbeck’s, with only Igor Thiago, Viktor Gyokeres and Junior Kroupi bettering his conversion rate of a little more than 23% last season, among players to have scored at least nine Premier League goals.

Excluding penalties, Welbeck also exceeded his expected goals total by almost two in the league last season. Here’s a look at some of his other statistics from the 2025/26 top flight.

articles.summary: Jordan Henderson is the latest midfielder on Chelsea's radar.
articles.content:
BREAKING: Chelsea in talks to sign Jordan Henderson from Brentford

Jordan Henderson is the latest midfielder on Chelsea's radar.

Last Update:

Chelsea are pushing to sign midfielder Jordan Henderson from Brentford, with the West London club currently leading the race for the former England captain.

Several Premier League clubs have expressed interest in the 36-year-old, but Chelsea are understood to be the frontrunners.

Brentford are prepared to allow Henderson to leave on a free transfer despite the midfielder still having a year remaining on the contract he signed after joining from Ajax last summer.

Henderson was part of Thomas Tuchel’s England squad at this summer’s World Cup, although his tournament was disrupted by injury.

The midfielder suffered a broken left arm after slipping while climbing over an advertising board during England’s last-16 victory over Mexico at the Estadio Azteca.

Chelsea’s pursuit of Henderson continues a noticeable shift in transfer strategy. After prioritising younger signings in recent years, the club have increasingly explored moves for established and experienced players during the current window.

In midfield, Chelsea have already sanctioned the departure of Andrey Santos, who joined Manchester United in a deal worth up to £50m this summer.

Henderson featured regularly for Brentford last season, making 22 Premier League starts and a further 10 appearances from the bench.

The veteran midfielder began his career at Sunderland before completing a move to Liverpool in 2011. During a 12-year spell at Anfield, Henderson established himself as one of the club’s most influential figures, captaining Liverpool to both Premier League and Champions League success while making 492 appearances in all competitions.

He left Liverpool for Saudi Pro League side Al Ettifaq in 2023, a move that attracted significant scrutiny due to his previous support of the LGBTQ+ community.

Chelsea are currently continuing their pre-season preparations in Australia, where they are scheduled to face Western Sydney Wanderers and Tottenham before travelling to Hong Kong to take on Juventus.

articles.title: Diomande’s former coach reveals rapid rise to top as Real Madrid transfer edges closer
articles.summary: Yan Diomande is set to complete a transfer to Real Madrid. His former coach always knew he would make it to the top.
articles.content:
Diomande’s former coach reveals rapid rise to top as Real Madrid transfer edges closer

Yan Diomande is set to complete a transfer to Real Madrid. His former coach always knew he would make it to the top.

Last Update:

During an international break in 2025, Leganes were preparing to face Real Madrid at the Santiago Bernabeu when an unknown 18-year-old winger from Ivory Coast, who had arrived injured to join the club’s reserve side in January, was unexpectedly handed his senior debut.

Former Leganes manager Borja Jimenez, now in charge of Al Ahli in Qatar, has recalled the moment he first realised the teenager’s potential.

“The first time I heard about Yan was when Jeff Luhnow, the owner of Leganes, showed me a homemade YouTube video of him,” Jimenez said.

“He was 16 years old and playing in one of the club’s academies in the United States. Jeff said to me: ‘We have the new Messi.’ I was amazed by what I saw.”

Jimenez’s first in-person look at Diomande came during a training match against the reserve team in the build-up to the Bernabeu trip.

“I hadn’t seen him properly before,” he explained.

“In his first action he beat a defender with ease. Then he did it again. Next he raced onto a through ball with an incredible first touch. Then he cut inside and fired into the top corner.

“After five or six moments like that, I called the reserve-team coach and told him: ‘Take Yan off now because the next challenge is going to be a bad tackle. Tomorrow he’s training with us.'”

Table of Contents

First impressions catch the eye

Diomande only played 45 minutes that day as he was still recovering from injury, but Jimenez believed it was enough.

“He was so much better than first-team players that it was starting to create tension. I didn’t want anyone to kick him.”

Before Diomande joined first-team training, Jimenez offered him some advice.

“I didn’t need to tell him how to play football. I spoke to him about behaviour,” he said.

“I told him to keep doing exactly what he’d been doing, but to respect the senior players. Arrive first, leave last, help your team-mates and understand you’re the new player.

“It was his first experience with a senior squad and I wanted to guide him. He understood everything immediately.”

The winger also quickly impressed his new team-mates.

“We were walking back to the dressing room after training when Dani Raba came over and simply said: ‘This boy is good.’ I just smiled and agreed.”

A debut against Real Madrid

Diomande was immediately included in the squad to face Real Madrid.

“We had to try and win that match, and from the first moment we knew he was different,” Jimenez said.

“His first real action was a burst past Fede Valverde that ended with what we believed should have been a penalty. From that moment, Yan’s story wrote itself.”

Despite only spending around six weeks with Leganes’ first team, Diomande made a major impact.

“He was never intimidated, not even at the Bernabeu,” Jimenez added.

“If he’d arrived in January instead of later, I honestly believe we would have qualified for the Conference League instead of being relegated.

“He transformed us. He scored goals, created chances and completely changed the team.”

Value on the rise

Jimenez also revealed he always expected Diomande’s value to skyrocket.

“When clubs from abroad asked about him, some thought £17m was too expensive.

“I told them that within a year he would be worth two or three times that.”

Leipzig eventually signed Diomande for around £17m, and after just one outstanding season in Germany, the teenager is now valued between £87m and £104m, with his move to Madrid set to be completed in the coming days.

articles.title: Arsenal away kit 26/27: Watch video, full details on new shirt and strip
articles.summary: All you need to know about Arsenal's 2026/27 away kit
articles.content:
Arsenal away kit 26/27: Watch video, full details on new shirt and strip

All you need to know about Arsenal's 2026/27 away kit

Last Update:

Reigning Premier League champions Arsenal have released their new Adidas away shirt as part of the club’s kit for the 2026/27 season.

The shirt, which was announced in July, is a throwback to the Bruised Banana look Arsenal wore between 1991 and 1993 and celebrates the “stories that live behind the shirt”.

Ian Wright, who was a prolific Gunners hero during his time at the club between 1991 and 1998, is shown mimicking the signing of his first contract with Arsenal as part of the promotional material.

Declan Rice, Riccardo Calafiori, Chloe Kelly and musician Little Simz are among the stars to have shown off the kit. Here are the key details on the release.

Table of Contents

Arsenal away kit 2026/27 full design details

The kit has a navy base and a graphic design inspired by the geometric pattern that made the original so distinctive, according to the club.

Yellow tones accompany a crew-neck collar with red and yellow accents. “We’re all looking forward to playing in this kit,” defender Calafiori said.

“We know the impact the Bruised Banana has had on our supporters; you only have to see how many still wear it today to understand how much it means to the club.

“We’re proud to wear something with such history attached to it and use that as inspiration as we continue to push ourselves forward.

“It’s our turn to create our own legacy at the club. We’ve enjoyed so many amazing moments with our supporters but we’re hungry for more.

“We want to keep winning, keep creating special memories together and give our supporters even more reasons to be proud.”

Now a popular pundit, Wright was Arsenal’s top scorer in each of the seasons the Bruised Banana shirt featured in.

Arsenal won the FA Cup and EFL Cup in the second of those campaigns.

How to buy Arsenal 26/27 away kit

The kit is available from Arsenal’s online shop. “The boss gave me a call,” Rice says as part of his accompanying launch video.

The England international is then seen taking a phone call from head coach Mikel Arteta by answering: “Hello, mate – how are you?”

“I just couldn’t say no to the shirt,” the 27-year-old then adds.

How much does the 26/27 Arsenal away kit cost?

The women’s and men’s Arsenal replica shirt is £85 or £90 for a long-sleeved version, while the authentic versions start at £120, with personalised or player names and numbers available at an additional cost.

Youth shirts start at £60. A baby kit is available for £40. The shorts cost between £30 and £38.

Accompanying socks cost between £16 and £20. A range of other clothing and items in the away colours are available, including bags and footballs.

When does Arsenal’s 2026/27 Premier League season start?

Arsenal face Manchester City in the Community Shield at Wembley Stadium on August 16 at 15:00 BST (10:00 ET / 07:00 PT).

Arteta’s team host the first match of the Premier League season against promoted visitors. Here are the key details.

articles.title: Yan Diomande back at RB Leipzig as Real Madrid increase offer for Ivory Coast winger
articles.summary: Real Madrid have upped their bid for Ivory Coast winger Yan Diomande as a potential replacement for Arsenal target Vinicius Jr
articles.content:
Yan Diomande back at RB Leipzig as Real Madrid increase offer for Ivory Coast winger

Real Madrid have upped their bid for Ivory Coast winger Yan Diomande as a potential replacement for Arsenal target Vinicius Jr

Last Update:

Yan Diomande is back at RB Leipzig and undergoing performance tests on Monday despite his future remaining up in the air.

The 19-year-old Ivory Coast international is reported to have agreed terms with Real Madrid but there remains no club-to-club agreement just yet.

Sky Germany claim an initial £85million bid has been rejected by Leipzig but a fresh offer today of £98m has seen talks resume. It is thought that if Madrid increase that to around £102m then Diomande would become a Real Madrid player.

That would represent a remarkable return for Leipzig who bought the winger from Leganes 12 months ago having met his release clause of £17m.

If he does move to the Santiago Bernabeu, Diomande would become the most expensive African player in history, surpassing the £72m Arsenal paid for Nicolas Pepe in 2019.

Diomande back in Germany as Madrid watch on

While the deal continues to advance slowly, Diomande was back in Germany today to be assessed following his exertions with Ivory Coast at the World Cup.

The teenager made four appearances in the United States, Canada and Mexico but largely underwhelmed as the Ivorians lost to Norway at the round of 32 stage.

Diomande’s potential move to Madrid could have a knock-on effect on the future of current star Vinicius Jr, who has been strongly linked with Arsenal in recent days.

The Athletic’s David Ornstein has indicated that the Premier League champions have made enquiries over a move for the Brazilian, although talks are said to be at an early stage.

The Brazilian has been linked with an exit from the Bernabeu after entering the final year of his contract, and Madrid’s move for Diomande – who like Vinicius is a left-winger – would suggest they are preparing for life without the two-time Champions League winner.

Arsenal are on the lookout for a new left-sided forward following Leandro Trossard’s departure, with the Gunners missing out on England international Morgan Rogers who moved to London rivals Chelsea from Aston Villa.

articles.title: BREAKING: Chelsea make move for former Arsenal and Manchester United striker Welbeck
articles.summary: Brighton's Danny Welbeck has emerged as a surprise target for Chelsea
articles.content:
BREAKING: Chelsea make move for former Arsenal and Manchester United striker Welbeck

Brighton's Danny Welbeck has emerged as a surprise target for Chelsea

Last Update:

Chelsea are exploring a move for Brighton striker Danny Welbeck, according to a report in The Athletic.

Welbeck has been among the best English centre-forwards in the Premier League for over a decade and shows no signs of slowing down despite being 35 years of age, appearing in 37 top-flight games last season and scoring 13 goals.

More importantly, he has the experience and dressing room influence that new Blues boss Xabi Alonso would like at Stamford Bridge.

Welbeck pursuit reinforces belief Alonso is targeting experience

Alonso attempted to bring Sunderland captain Granit Xhaka to the club earlier in the window only for the Wearsiders to rebuff their interest while free agent England international John Stones is also a reported target.

Welbeck has 12 months left on his deal at Brighton, for whom he has scored 51 goals in 201 games since joining from Watford in 2020. It has been an Indian summer for the Manchester-born forward who came through the ranks at Old Trafford, scoring 29 goals in 142 games before moving to the Emirates where he managed 32 goals in 126 appearances.

Chelsea have invested heavily again this summer, signing the likes of Morgan Rogers and Marco Palestra but they still lack a top-class number nine.

Welbeck could fill that void in the short-term while the club focus on a longer-term alternative.

Joao Pedro is the only forward that Alonso is eager to keep with Liam Delap, Emmanuel Emegha, Marc Guiu and Nicolas Jackson all available for transfer.

Should the move go through, Welbeck would be the latest in a long line of players and coaches to follow the well-trodden path from Brighton to Chelsea, following on from Marc Cucurella, Robert Sanchez, Moises Caicedo, Pedro, Facundo Buonanotte and Graham Potter.

Chelsea are in action tomorrow when they face A-League side Western Sydney Wanderers in Australia.

articles.title: Neymar hits back at ‘malicious fake news’: ‘I won’t accept that total lie’
articles.summary: Neymar scored twice for Santos but earned a second ban of the season
articles.content:
Neymar hits back at ‘malicious fake news’: ‘I won’t accept that total lie’

Neymar scored twice for Santos but earned a second ban of the season

Last Update:

Neymar says a report claiming he mistreated teammates while playing for club side Santos on Saturday is the result of “lies on the internet” by people who “don’t know football”.

Brazil record scorer Neymar “bothered a large portion” of Santos’ squad by “going overboard in the tone” of his remarks to Gabriel Bontempo and Joao Ananias, according to Globo, who said both the midfielder and defender later denied there had been an issue.

Citing sources, the outlet alleged Neymar did not take part in a scheduled training session on Sunday but briefly attended to have coffee and take photos before leaving without permission, leading to board members visiting Santos’ base to investigate the situation.

“I’m seeing some stuff coming out saying that I called out the young players in the locker room,” Neymar said in an Instagram video.

“That is a total lie. Whoever passed that along, please don’t do that. Don’t do that – don’t lie. Don’t lie – you can ask anyone you want who’s in this dressing room.”

Table of Contents

Neymar Instagram video: What Santos striker said

Neymar denied he had targeted 21-year-old Bontempo or 19-year-old Ananias during relegation-threatened Santos’ 2-2 home draw with rock-bottom Chapecoense.

“Good Sunday to everyone,” said the 34-year-old. “It wasn’t the Sunday we wanted, but that’s it: heads up and keep working.

“There was accountability for the team… we held each other accountable because we’re competitive, we want to win, we want to succeed.

“But there was no calling out of the young players at all. I won’t accept that. From now on, I won’t accept you guys putting out these lies on the internet.

“Got it? We’re in this together, and that’s that. It’s on us. And another thing: if we do have to hold each other accountable inside the dressing room, regardless of who it is, then that’s normal in football.

“It’s normal for a group that wants to win. You guys making these malicious, fake news articles don’t know anything.

“You don’t know football and you’re not part of – and have never been part of – a squad.”

The former Al-Hilal, Paris Saint-Germain and Barcelona striker explained that he had “talked” with “all of” his teammates as part of their desire to win, namechecking Gabriel Brazao, Lucas Verissimo, Willian Arao and Gabriel.

The video ended with a clip showing clouds from an aeroplane window, accompanied by the best-known lyric of Bob Marley’s Three Little Birds: “Don’t worry about a thing”.

Neymar: Brazil superstar denies news report

The report said the alleged “episode” was “yet another friction point leading to discomfort among a large part of the Santos squad with the star player”, claiming Neymar has “annoyed” players and executives.

It said Neymar’s teammates had been “unimpressed” by his participation in a poker tournament on Tuesday – the same day they travelled to Venezuela to beat Universidad Central 4-1 in the first leg of their Copa Sudamericana knockout round play-off tie.

Some sections of the Brazilian press criticised Neymar at the time he took part in the poker tournament, which took place while he was returning to full fitness following the World Cup 2026.

Making his comeback after the finals in the game against Chapecoense, two-goal Neymar celebrated by pretending to deal poker cards, having explained at the time of the reports that he had trained with Santos and been given permission to pursue his pastime.

Santos vs Chapecoense: Neymar goals

Neymar exchanged a one-two with Argentinian winger Alvaro Barreal before putting the eight-time Brazilian champions ahead in the 36th minute of the match, but they are a point above the drop zone after being held by opponents who are at the foot of Serie A by eight points.

Marcinho’s equaliser after the break – allowed following a Video Assistant Referee review – and Joao Ananias’ 62nd-minute own goal gave the visitors a surprise lead.

Neymar, who was booked for shoving Bruno Tubarao, then kept his cool to salvage a draw and keep his side 14th, a point above the relegation zone.

The altercation with Tubarao led to Neymar’s third successive booking in Santos matches and has earned him a suspension.

Neymar Santos stats

Neymar now has six goals in this season’s Serie A, finding the net for his club for the first time since May 10 on his first Santos appearance since May 17.

He has been cautioned in four of his last five games for club and country and has a total of nine yellow cards in 2026, which matches the number of goals he has scored in all competitions.

Still the world’s most expensive player from his £200m move from Barcelona to PSG in August 2017, Neymar is under contract with Santos until the end of the calendar year.

World Cup 2026: Neymar returns from Brazil cameo

A surprise inclusion in Brazil’s squad following a succession of injury issues, Neymar missed his country’s opening draw with Morocco and subsequent win over Haiti because of a calf problem.

Brazil used Neymar briefly during their win over Scotland in their third group stage match but kept him on the bench for their 2-1 comeback victory against Japan in the last 32.

Head coach Carlo Ancelotti again introduced Neymar as a second-half substitute in Brazil’s 2-1 last-16 defeat to Norway.

The Selecao conceded twice with Neymar on the pitch, meaning his added-time penalty counted for nothing as the five-time champions were knocked out.

When is Neymar’s next game? Santos fixtures

With 19 matches of the Brazilian season played, only bottom two clubs Chapecoense and Remo have fewer wins than Santos’ total of five.

Neymar could be involved in their return match at home to Universidad Central on Wednesday.

They then visit Sao Paulo in the league, play a two-legged Brazilian Cup tie against Remo and host Athletico-PR and travel to Vasco in the top flight.

Neymar Brazil stats

The 2021 Copa America Best Player has 130 caps and broke Pele’s record by scoring the 78th of his 80 international goals during Brazil’s World Cup qualifier against Bolivia in September 2023, but ruptured his anterior cruciate ligament against Uruguay the following month.

After missing two games at the 2022 World Cup with an ankle injury, Neymar produced two goals and one assists but was part of a team knocked out by Croatia in the quarter-finals.

The defeat to Norway ensured he has never played beyond the last eight of the tournament, having been ever-present and contributed two goals and two assists before Brazil were knocked out at that stage by Belgium in 2018.

At his first World Cup in 2014, Neymar finished on four goals and one assist in five games but missed Brazil’s 7-1 semi-final defeat to Germany and 3-0 third-placed match loss to the Netherlands through injury.

articles.title: FIFA chief Infantino accuses media of ‘spreading hate’ and lauds success of 2026 World Cup in bizarre rant
articles.summary: Gianni Infantino has taken aim at FIFA's critics with a lengthy rant that highlighted the positives of the 2026 World Cup
articles.content:
FIFA chief Infantino accuses media of ‘spreading hate’ and lauds success of 2026 World Cup in bizarre rant

Gianni Infantino has taken aim at FIFA's critics with a lengthy rant that highlighted the positives of the 2026 World Cup

Last Update:

FIFA president Gianni Infantino has launched a blistering attack on the media for “spreading hate and false rumours” and highlighted the success of the 2026 World Cup.

Infantino lashed out at those “behind their pens and papers, behind their screens” and lauded his organisation for “delivering the most outstanding World Cup”.

The World Cup came to an end last weekend with Spain beating Argentina 1-0 in a final marred by the South Americans’ appalling behaviour in New Jersey.

It was a disappointing end to a tournament that featured plenty of controversies, from Iran’s restricted movement around the United States to the decision to suspend a red card handed out to US striker Folarin Balogun following the intervention of Donald Trump.

In a statement on FIFA’s website, Infantino wrote: “To everyone who missed our beautiful game, the emotions, the celebrations, the laughter, the crying, the deception, and the joy. To all of you who missed watching kids, babies, grandparents, and parents come together for the beautiful game, I say sorry that the matches are now over and sorry that you missed all that joy and togetherness. Sorry that you were so consumed by hate and criticism that you missed it all.

“To those behind their pens and papers, behind their screens spreading hate and false rumours, I want to say that while you are sitting behind, we at FIFA are on the front lines organising, working hard, and delivering the best show in the world.

“While you divide, we unite. Every city was packed with fans from all around the globe. While they celebrated, you were busy planting seeds of hate.”

Table of Contents

Infantino claims FIFA united Iran and the USA

Iran exited at the group stage and, afterwards, complained of being “oppressed” following a US ruling that meant they could only fly into the country from their training base in Mexico the day before a game and then leave immediately after.

The US has been bombing Iran for several months and the country’s homeland security secretary Markwayne Mullin was delighted when they failed to reach the round of 32.

At the time he said: “I was so happy when we were able to pull their visas and said they could leave US soil, and I might’ve sung a song or two or maybe even danced a happy dance. I’m very happy they’re going back because there wasn’t a single team that we dealt with more than them.”

On Iran, Infantino said: “While you [the media] spread hatred, we worked tirelessly to unite two countries at war. Iran entered the United States without incident or conflict. When the Iranian team began playing, all the chants against them turned into a single song. The fans became the country, they became the team, and they stood behind Team Melli. This is the power of football. The Iranian team received visas to enter because football is about peace. It’s not about politics. Football is about unity, not division. Football is bigger than hate and discrimination.”

Infantino accuses critics of hypocrisy over Balogun

Infantino also sought to defend the fiasco surrounding Balogun, who remained the only player at the tournament to have his red card suspended by FIFA’s disciplinary committee. Trump later admitted to calling Infantino and asking for the case to be reviewed in a bid to enable the player to face Belgium in the round of 16.

Trump, who was awarded FIFA’s inaugural Peace Prize last December, got his way and Balogun played in the States’ 4-1 defeat to the Red Devils.

The Norwegian Football Federation is set to make a formal complaint over the matter but Infantino claims it was normal procedure.

He said: “Your dissatisfaction with a few decisions made by the competent authorities is understandable, but please refer to public records: such decisions are common in some of the most important leagues.

“Indeed, ‘arguable’ referees’ decisions or ‘strange’ disciplinary rulings such as for instance potentially mistaken red or yellow cards or subsequent decisions not to ban players in certain situations are routine and widely accepted in some of the biggest leagues worldwide.

“It’s curious that the same countries employing these practices are the ones criticising.”

FIFA have found peace – Infantino

There were also accusations Lionel Messi’s Argentina were given several favourable decisions as they looked to retain the trophy they won in Qatar in 2022.

Infantino remained unmoved and delivered another parting shot at the media, adding: “To those spending their time and energy hating us, please take a moment to reflect, meditate, pray, or watch a football match and truly observe the faces, the eyes, the emotions.

“Because only our beautiful game can deliver such an extraordinary show, a show where everyone becomes one and reconnects as humans.

“To the pens and papers, to all the screens, may you find love and peace where the people behind you couldn’t.

“May you find peace; we at FIFA have found ours and we deliver it, by delivering the most outstanding FIFA World Cup. May football rise above all hate.”

articles.title: Chelsea are not done in the transfer market, says Alonso, who hatches plan to pair Rogers and Palmer
articles.summary: Chelsea have had another busy window but there is still work to do, according to boss Xabi Alonso
articles.content:
Chelsea are not done in the transfer market, says Alonso, who hatches plan to pair Rogers and Palmer

Chelsea have had another busy window but there is still work to do, according to boss Xabi Alonso

Last Update:

Xabi Alonso says Chelsea’s work in the transfer market is not yet done and is confident the club has a “clear plan” for the way forward.

Chelsea’s philosophy has often appeared muddled over recent seasons due to a huge turnover in players and a focus on prioritising youth over experience. The results on the field have been underwhelming and they head into 2026/27 without European football.

Alonso is an exciting appointment as head coach and he has been backed this summer with the signings of Morgan Rogers, Marco Palestra, Geovany Quenda and Emmanuel Emegha. France international Maxence Lacroix is also poised to move to Stamford Bridge from Crystal Palace.

The Spaniard hinted there could be more arrivals as well as several exits as the club looks to trim a squad that now carries almost 40 senior professionals.

“We need to know that there will probably still be some movement,” said Alonso, speaking from Sydney on the club’s pre-season tour.

“We need to be flexible and quick to act. The main thing is that we have a clear idea, a clear plan that we have built.

“It will probably change before the transfer window closes.

“We want a squad with the right balance between quality and mentality.

“Those things need to match in terms of maturity, but I think we are starting the new season with good energy. That’s important.”

Table of Contents

Alonso says Rogers will make instant impact at Chelsea

Rogers is the headline arrival of the summer so far, the England international joining from Aston Villa in a £117m move that makes him the most expensive British player of all time.

“In that position we needed an important player and I’m sure there were not many better options than Morgan Rogers,” Alonso said.

“You need players who can have that almost instant impact and I’m sure Morgan won’t need much time to adapt to the club, the system and his team-mates.

“That was the idea, to get a top player, and Morgan is one of them.”

Palmer and Rogers can work together – Chelsea boss Alonso

Rogers generally plays in the number 10 position currently occupied by his close friend Cole Palmer but Alonso claims to have a plan that will see both men in the starting XI.

“I have an idea. I can see them linking really well,” Alonso said.

“We need to have a good mix. If we get that balance right and those special players in the right positions, with good control, then we will be more competitive with and without the ball.

“One of his [Rogers’] best qualities is that he is flexible. In that pocket position, close to the striker, close to our No 10, but he’s played as well on the right side, but more coming from the left.

“He feels he is enjoying his game, his flow, and I am sure he will have good connections with the other players around him. If we get those connections right, that will be a great step forward in the quality of our game.”

articles.title: Revealed: The top 10 most expensive Premier League signings of all time adjusted for inflation
articles.summary: Morgan Rogers and Elliot Anderson are outside the top 30 transfers
articles.content:
Revealed: The top 10 most expensive Premier League signings of all time adjusted for inflation

Morgan Rogers and Elliot Anderson are outside the top 30 transfers

Last Update:

Morgan Rogers’ £117m switch from Aston Villa to Chelsea and Elliot Anderson’s £116 million move from Nottingham Forest to Manchester City each broke the record for the most expensive British player of all time in July 2026.

New figures, though, show that neither transfer has threatened to match the most expensive signings ever by Premier League when they are adjusted for inflation.

Football finance experts Valuball have compiled a list of deals in today’s money based on a range of comprehensively calculated data.

Here’s how they rank the most expensive Premier League club signings ever, plus a look at where more recent deals stand on the all-time list.

Table of Contents

10) Paul Pogba – Manchester United, £141.6m (£89.3m)

Originally part of United’s academy, Pogba left United for Juventus as a 19-year-old in 2012 and returned from the Italian club for a world-record fee in 2016, when Jose Mourinho saw him as integral to his vision of success.

The Europa League and EFL Cup titles of his first season were Pogba’s only trophies at the club, leaving on a free transfer in 2022, having also won the World Cup with France in 2018.

9) Dwight Yorke – Manchester United, £144.7m (£12.6m)

“If I’d had a gun at the time, I would have shot him,” then-Aston Villa manager John Gregory said of Dwight Yorke’s request to leave the club, resulting in the striker becoming United’s then-record signing in August 1998.

Yorke won the Premier League Player of the Season and golden boot alongside a treble with his new club the following season, becoming a league champion again in each of the next two campaigns.

The Trinidad and Tobago international was exiled after a training ground row with United boss Sir Alex Ferguson in September 2001 and moved to Blackburn Rovers for £2 million the following July, later winning the A-League with Sydney and Championship with Sunderland.

8) Andriy Shevchenko – Chelsea, £152.6m (£30.8m)

Mourinho described the signing of Shevchenko, who had won the 2004 Ballon d’Or among a stack of individual and collective honours at Milan, as a “dream” in 2006.

Ukraine all-time top scorer Shevchenko had averaged under a goal every five league matches by the time he left for Dynamo Kyiv in 2009, released from his £121,000-a-week contract 11 months early under Carlo Ancelotti.

7) Andy Cole – Manchester United, £153.8m (£7m)

Newcastle fans protested when the extraordinarily prolific Cole made a shock move to United in January 1997, breaking the British transfer record in a swap for winger Keith Gillespie.

Cole was part of United’s treble-winning 1998/99 squad and won four more Premier League titles and the FA Cup twice, with only Alan Shearer and Yorke producing more goals or direct goal involvements in the top flight than the England international during his time with the club.

No player has ever scored more goals for a Premier League team without taking any penalties, but Cole’s dissatisfaction with being left out by United led to him joining Blackburn for £7.6m in December 2001.

6) Dennis Bergkamp – Arsenal, £156m (£7.5m)

Bergkamp’s addition as Arsenal’s record signing in 1995 came a year before the arrival of transformative manager Arsene Wenger, who has justifiably called the Gunners icon “the first push” of the club “into the modern, international era”.

The subject of a statue outside the Emirates Stadium, Bergkamp won the Premier League three times and FA Cup four times before ending his career at Arsenal and kicking off the first match at their new home in his testimonial against former club Ajax in 2006.

5) Fernando Torres – Chelsea, £157.8m (£50m)

Chelsea broke the British transfer record in January 2011 for Torres, a EURO 2008 and World Cup 2010 winner with Spain who had scored 81 times in 142 matches across three-and-a-half years with Liverpool.

Notably less prolific than he had been for the Reds and Atletico Madrid, Torres still won the Champions League and FA Cup in 2011/12 and the 2012/13 Europa League, as well as contributing 35 assists before initially leaving to join Milan on loan in 2014.

4) Stan Collymore – Liverpool, £176.8m (£8.5m)

Swiftly breaking the British record set by Cole’s switch, Liverpool swooped for Nottingham Forest goal machine Collymore in July 1995 and were rewarded with a return of 102 goals in two seasons from the England international and strike partner Robbie Fowler.

Collymore was perceived to have attitude problems and has admitted he regrets leaving Anfield for boyhood club Aston Villa two years later, having had a tricky relationship with manager Roy Evans and found his place threatened by the emergence of teenage sensation Michael Owen.

3) Juan Sebastian Veron – Manchester United, £178.5m (£28.1m)

United made Veron the first non-European to break the British record when Sir Alex Ferguson decided to sign the Argentina international who had established himself as one of the best midfielders in the world with Lazio.

Veron won the 2002/03 Premier League but never hit his previous heights with United, who recouped little more than half the fee they had paid when he left two years later for a peripheral spell at Chelsea. The two-time South American Footballer of the Year has said he wishes he had stayed at Old Trafford.

2) Rio Ferdinand – Manchester United, £198.5m (£33.3m)

Leeds paid West Ham £18m to make Ferdinand the world’s most expensive defender in November 2000 and United followed suit to sign the 23-year-old from the Whites in July 2002.

The hall-of-famer and England stalwart won the Premier League six times, the 2007/08 Champions League and the EFL Cup twice during a 12-year career with the club, as well as scoring United’s last goal under Ferguson.

1) Alan Shearer – Newcastle, £236.9m (£15m)

A huge crowd massed to celebrate Shearer’s symbolic return to his home city after Newcastle beat Manchester United to his signature in July 1996, shortly after he had reaffirmed his status as one of the best strikers in the world during England’s run to the EURO semi-finals.

Despite failing to add to the Premier League title he won with former club Blackburn Rovers, the Newcastle trialist as a boy won the top-flight golden boot in 1997 and remains the all-time record scorer in the division thanks to his time on Tyneside until 2007, briefly returning as interim manager in 2009.

Most expensive Premier League signings: The top 40

Rogers is 29th and Anderson 32nd as the two players to have joined the top 40 this summer.

At 15th, Alexander Isak’s move to Liverpool last year puts the former Newcastle striker well above both, eight ahead of another Reds signing for 2025/26, Florian Wirtz.

All data: Valuball

articles.summary: Watch highlights as Premier League clubs start pre-season
articles.content:
Pre season friendly matches today: Reports, results, goals from across Europe

Watch highlights as Premier League clubs start pre-season

Last Update:

Top clubs from across Europe continued their preparations for the 2026/27 season by playing friendly fixtures on Sunday.

Premier League side Nottingham Forest drew with Portuguese top-flight opponents Vitoria and reigning Italian champions Inter won as part of their training camp in Italy.

Serie A clubs Napoli and Roma were also in action, Paulo Dybala scoring a spectacular free-kick for I Giallorossi.

Dutch giants Ajax beat Burnley, who were relegated to the Championship last season, at the Johan Cruyff Arena.

Table of Contents

Nottingham Forest vs Vitoria: Igor Jesus scores

Forest took a first-half lead as part of their training camp in Portugal when Igor Jesus scored following an Ola Aina attempt.

Vitoria, who finished ninth last season, earned a 1-1 draw through Miguel Nogueira’s second-half penalty after Tyler Bindon’s challenge on Zeega.

Forest have not made their line-up public.

Cannes vs Roma: Dybala double, Wesley red card

Paulo Dybala’s superb free-kick and assist for Donyell Malen to strike inside the box put Roma 2-0 ahead in Cannes, where Wesley received a second booking for Gian Piero Gasperini’s team during first-half added time.

Forward Dybala charged inside the box and slotted in his second after the break, but Julian Lopez’s glorious volley from a corner and finish from closer range launched the hosts’ comeback.

Brice Oggad’s added-time penalty – awarded for an Artem Dovbyk foul – completed the scoring in a 3-3 draw worthy of a city synonymous with the cinematic.

Roma starting XI: Mile Svilar, Gianluca Mancini, Evan Ndicka, Mario Hermoso, Devyne Rensch, Bryan Cristante, Muhammad Bah, Wesley, Paulo Dybala, Matias Soule, Donyell Malen

Napoli vs Carrarese: Hojlund goal helps Allegri off mark

Max Allegri won for the first time as Napoli manager with a 2-0 victory against second-tier side Carrarese in Carciato.

Matteo Politano struck the crossbar for the Serie A club early on and Fabio Abiuso followed suit at the other end before Rasmus Hojlund tapped in and Antonio Vergara converted a penalty during the first half.

Vergara, who has just signed a new deal until 2031, was withdrawn during the second period with a knee injury.

Napoli starting XI: Alex Meret, Giovanni Di Lorenzo, Amir Rrahmani, Luca Marianucci, Leonardo Spinazzola, Frank Anguissa, Stanislav Lobotka, Giacomo Raspadori, Matteo Politano, Rasmus Hojlund, Giovane

Ajax vs Burnley: Bouwman, Ouazane give hosts win

Michel Sanchez’s first home match as Ajax manager ended with a 2-1 win over Burnley, taking an early lead through 18-year-old defender Aaron Bouwman’s close-range strike.

Dutch forward Jaydon Banel equalised for Burnley with a deflection during the second half, but 17-year-old Amsterdammers midfielder Abdellah Ouazane tucked in the winner five minutes later.

Ajax starting XI: Joeri Heerkens, Anton Gaaei, Kian Fitz-Jim Bouwman, Youri Baas, Caio Henrique, Jinairo Johnson, Jorthy Mokio, Abdellah Ouazane, Maher Carrizo, Marcos Leonardo, Oliver Edvardsen

Burnley starting XI: Max Weiss, Kyle Walker, Connor Roberts, Bashir Humphreys, Lucas Pires, Josh Laurent, Aaron Ramsey, Hannibal Mejbri, Jacob Bruun Larsen, Marcus Edwards, Jaydon Banel

Rangers vs West Ham: Stalemate at Ibrox

Scottish title hopefuls Rangers and relegated Premier League side West Ham shared a 0-0 draw in front of more than 48,000 fans at Ibrox, including 2,600 visiting supporters.

Home goalkeeper Ivor Pandur denied James Ward-Prowse twice, with counterpart Mads Hermansen saving from Mohamed Diomande, Thelo Aasgaard, Tochi Chukwani and Lawrence Shankland.

Rangers starting XI: Ivor Pandur, Dujon Sterling, Ben Godfrey, Emmanuel Fernandez, Tuur Rommens, Cammy Devlin, Thelo Aasgaard, Findlay Curtis, Mohamed Diomande, Ryan Naderi, Adil Aouchiche, Djeidi Gassama

West Ham starting XI: Mads Hermansen, Kyle Walker-Peters, Konstantinos Mavropanos, Max Kilman, Oliver Scarles, Keiber Lamadrid, Mohamadou Kant, James Ward-Prowse, Jarrod Bowen, Taty Castellanos, Pablo Fornals

articles.title: Neymar: Watch goals video as Brazil icon cops ban on Santos return in striker’s first match since World Cup 2026
articles.summary: Neymar scored his first Santos goals for almost three months
articles.content:
Neymar: Watch goals video as Brazil icon cops ban on Santos return in striker’s first match since World Cup 2026

Neymar scored his first Santos goals for almost three months

Last Update:

Brazil record scorer Neymar rescued a point for Santos but incurred a suspension on his first appearance since the Selecao’s last-16 exit at the World Cup 2026.

Neymar exchanged a one-two with Argentinian winger Alvaro Barreal before putting the eight-time Brazilian champions ahead in the 36th minute, but they remain in relegation trouble after being held to a 2-2 draw at home to Chapecoense, who are bottom of Serie A by eight points.

Marcinho’s equaliser after the break – allowed following a Video Assistant Referee review – and Joao Ananias’ 62nd-minute own goal gave the visitors a surprise lead.

Neymar, who was booked for shoving Bruno Tubarao, then kept his cool to salvage a draw and keep his side 14th, a point above the relegation zone.

Table of Contents

Neymar: Santos goal celebration pokes fun at poker criticism

Neymar received criticism in the Brazilian press after he took part in a poker tournament while he was returning to full fitness following the World Cup.

The 34-year-old celebrated in his comeback match by pretending to deal poker cards, having explained at the time of the reports that he had trained with Santos and been given permission to pursue his pastime.

Former Al-Hilal, Paris-Saint-Germain and Barcelona playmaker Neymar now has six goals in this season’s Serie A, scoring his first club goals since May 10 on his first Santos appearance since May 17.

World Cup 2026: Neymar returns from Brazil cameo

A surprise inclusion in Brazil’s squad following a succession of injury issues, Neymar missed his country’s opening draw with Morocco and subsequent win over Haiti because of a calf problem.

Brazil used Neymar briefly during their win over Scotland in their third group stage match but kept him on the bench for their 2-1 comeback victory against Japan in the last 32.

Head coach Carlo Ancelotti again introduced Neymar as a second-half substitute in Brazil’s 2-1 last-16 defeat to Norway.

The Selecao conceded twice with Neymar on the pitch, meaning his added-time penalty counted for nothing as the five-time champions were knocked out.

When is Neymar’s next game? Santos fixtures

With 19 matches of the Brazilian season played, only bottom two clubs Chapecoense and Remo have fewer wins than Santos’ total of five.

Neymar could be involved in their Sudamerican knockout round play-off at home to Venezuelan club Universidad Central on Wednesday.

They then visit Sao Paulo in the league, play a two-legged Brazilian Cup tie against Remo and host Athletico-PR and travel to Vasco in the top flight.

Neymar Brazil stats

The 2021 Copa America Best Player has 130 caps and broke Pele’s record by scoring the 78th of his 80 international goals during Brazil’s World Cup qualifier against Bolivia in September 2023, but ruptured his anterior cruciate ligament against Uruguay the following month.

After missing two games at the 2022 World Cup with an ankle injury, Neymar produced two goals and one assists but was part of a team knocked out by Croatia in the quarter-finals.

The defeat to Norway ensured he has never played beyond the last eight of the tournament, having been ever-present and contributed two goals and two assists before Brazil were knocked out at that stage by Belgium in 2018.

At his first World Cup in 2014, Neymar finished on four goals and one assist in five games but missed Brazil’s 7-1 semi-final defeat to Germany and 3-0 third-placed match loss to the Netherlands through injury.

Neymar salary, wages, contract

Neymar reportedly signed an initial six-month contract with Santos, which he has since extended until the end of the last Brazilian season in December.

The Champions League winner is said to have had a deal worth £125m a year with previous club Al-Hilal, who he joined from PSG for around £77.6m plus add-ons in August 2023.

articles.title: Tottenham: Inter Milan chief confirms interest in Romero as De Zerbi says transfer window ‘not done yet’ and updates on Bergvall, Maddison, Kudus and Kulusevski
articles.summary: De Zerbi spoke after Tottenham's 2-0 win over Auckland
articles.content:
Tottenham: Inter Milan chief confirms interest in Romero as De Zerbi says transfer window ‘not done yet’ and updates on Bergvall, Maddison, Kudus and Kulusevski

De Zerbi spoke after Tottenham's 2-0 win over Auckland

Last Update:

Inter Milan sporting director Piero Ausilo has confirmed the club are looking to sign Tottenham captain Cristian Romero.

The Serie A champions are looking to sign a new central defender and Romero is believed to be one of their top targets, having also been linked with free agent John Stones.

Spurs manager De Zerbi previously opened the door for any wantaway players to leave the club amid doubts over the futures of Romero and midfielder Lucas Bergvall.

Inter have now confirmed their interest in the Argentina international, but indicated it will be a complex deal to get done.

Ausilo told Sky Italy: “It’s definitely a deal we are trying to sign with the player and the club [Tottenham]. These things take some time but there’s definitely interest. Let’s see.”

Table of Contents

De Zerbi: We must find solution to Bergvall situation

Midfielder Bergvall is believed to want out of Spurs after limited game time since De Zerbi was appointed in March, and De Zerbi admitted after Spurs’ 2-0 win over Auckland on Sunday that they need to resolve the Sweden international’s future either way.

“I have not spoken with Lucas yet. I will in the next days and we will make the best decision for the club, for Lucas, for me, for every one of us. Without problems, Lucas is a big, big talent,” the Italian said.

“There will be a big competition to play because at the end, I think we will be two players for each position. If he wants to stay, I will be happy.

“Otherwise, we have to find a new solution with Johan Lange, with Vinai. It’s not my business after the decision to leave.”

Spurs not done in transfer window

Spurs have been one of the most active teams in the transfer window, splashing out over £200million on Matheus Fernandes, Sandro Tonali, Marcos Senesi, Jan Paul van Hecke, Andy Robertson and Martin Dubravka so far.

De Zerbi insisted the North Londoners are not done yet as they look to reshape their squad, with at least one new forward thought to be a priority.

“It is not finished yet, our transfer market,” De Zerbi added.

“I think we can be happier at the end of this transfer market, because I spoke a lot to the owner, the board and they want to build a very strong team for this season but to make the base for the future to become great again.”

De Zerbi explains Maddison absence vs Auckland

De Zerbi named a youthful starting XI for the first pre-season game of their tour in New Zealand and Australia, with Dane Scarlett and Richarlison on target in a 2-0 win.

James Maddison was one of the players who did not feature at Eden Park, with the midfielder returning from an ACL injury towards the end of last season.

Explaining the England international’s absence, De Zerbi said: “He’s not working the last five days, I think, like Udogie, but they have not a big problem, just to stay focused, don’t take any risks and then for the next game, the next friendly game against Sydney.

“Maybe we play with Tonali, with other players, maybe, we’ve got to see.”

Kudus close to returning

De Zerbi also said Mohammed Kudus is close to returning to action for Spurs, having not played since a season-ending injury in January.

“Kudus is very close,” De Zerbi said. “I think when we come back to London he will be available to start working with us. It’s a great thing for us. Kudus is another important player.”

De Zerbi also gave an update on goalkeeper Guglielmo Vicario and Dejan Kulusevski.

“Vicario is injured, not a big injury, but he needs to stay one week in London,” he said.

“Kulusevski, we have to see in the next couple of weeks. He’s another important player. After one season, one complete season, without a game, we have to analyse better and better, don’t take risks, first of all for him and then for us.”

articles.title: MLS round-up: Heung-Min Son scores again for LAFC and Luis Suarez hits panenka winner in Inter Miami win, Griezmann and Lewandowski fire blanks
articles.summary: Heung-Min Son has scored three goals in three games since the World Cup
articles.content:
MLS round-up: Heung-Min Son scores again for LAFC and Luis Suarez hits panenka winner in Inter Miami win, Griezmann and Lewandowski fire blanks

Heung-Min Son has scored three goals in three games since the World Cup

Last Update:

The Major League Soccer season continued on Saturday night as the race for the play-offs began to heat up.

LAFC continued their fine form by going level at the top of the Western Conference with a 4-0 win over Sporting Kansas City, which saw Heung-Min Son score for the third straight game. Meanwhile, Inter Miami kept up the pace at the top of the Eastern Conference with a 1-0 win over Montreal courtesy of Luis Suarez’s late chipped penalty.

With the likes of Robert Lewandowski and Antoine Griezmann also featuring for their sides, catch up on all the MLS action from Saturday in the United States.

Table of Contents

LAFC 4-0 Sporting KC: Son scores for third-straight game

Ex-Tottenham captain Son continued his excellent form since a disappointing group-stage exit with North Korea at the World Cup by opening the scoring as LAFC brezzed past Sporting KC.

The 34-year-old found the net inside five minutes, with Denis Bouanga scored twice either side of a David Martinez strike to scure a comprehensive win for the Western Conference hopefuls.

LA’s victory takes them level with Vancoucer and San Jose at the top of the Western Conference, although their challengers both have games in hand over them.

Montreal 0-1 Inter Miami: Suarez scored panenka

Luis Suarez’s sublime chipped penalty earned Inter Miami a 1-0 win over Montreal to stay within touching distance with Nashville at the top of the Eastern Conference.

The Uruguayan, who also scored twice in a 3-2 win over Chicago Fire earlier this week, showed the coolness from the spot to earn the Herons an important win, with new signing Casemiro also making his debut following his move earlier this week.

Miami, who are still without Lionel Messi after the World Cup, look on course to reach the play-offs as they went just two points behind leaders Nashville, who were beaten 1-0 by Orlando City.

Elsewhere in MLS

Elsewhere, the wait for Robert Lewandowski’s first goal since joining Chicago Fire went on as they lost 3-1 away to New York City FC.

Antoine Griezmann is also still hunting for his first goal for Orlando City, although they did grab a huge win on his home debut over Nashville.

Timo Werner missed a penalty for San Jose Earthquakes as they drew 1-1 with LA Galaxy, with Reid Roberts cancellong out Joseph Painstill’s opener.

New England also secured an impressive 4-1 win over Atlanta United, with Carles Gil, Dor Turgeman, Peyton Miller and Brooklyn Raines on target before Miguel Almiron grabbed a consolation late on.

articles.title: Real Madrid in ‘pole position’ for Liverpool target Diomande after Vinicius Junior linked to Arsenal
articles.summary: Diomande looks set to join Real Madrid
articles.content:
Real Madrid in ‘pole position’ for Liverpool target Diomande after Vinicius Junior linked to Arsenal

Diomande looks set to join Real Madrid

Last Update:

Real Madrid are reportedly in pole position to sign winger Yan Diomande from RB Leipzig, according to Sky in Germany.

Real look the most likely club for the 19-year-old Ivory Coast international after agreeing terms, although an £85million bid has been rejected by the German club.

Diomande has previously been linked with Champions League winners Paris Saint-Germain – with whom he is also said to have agreed terms – while Liverpool are also thought to be keen on landing the youngster.

Leipzig are said to want significantly more than £85m for their prized asset, who scored 13 goals and assisted 10 last season, which has reportedly put Liverpool off the move.

Real have had a busy transfer window under Jose Mourinho so far, bringing in Marc Cucurella, Bernardo Silva, Ibrahima Konate and Denzel Dumfries this summer.

Arsenal explore move for Vinicius Jr

Real’s move for Diomande could end up having a knock-on effect on the future of current star Vinicius Junior, who has been strongly linked with Arsenal in recent days.

The Athletic’s David Ornstein has indicated that the Premier League champions have made enquiries over a move for the Brazilian, although talks are said to be at an early stage.

The Brazilian has been linked with an exit from the Bernabeu after entering the final year of his contract, and Real’s move for Diomande – who like Vinicius is a left-winger – would suggest they are preparing for life without the two-time Champions League winner.

Arsenal are on the lookout for a new left-winger following Leandro Trossard’s departure, with the Gunners missing out on England international Morgan Rogers who moved to London rivals Chelsea from Aston Villa.

articles.title: Premier League pre season friendly matches today: Reports, results, goals as Aston Villa lose, Hull win and Everton held by Bolton
articles.summary: Watch highlights as Premier League clubs start pre-season
articles.content:
Premier League pre season friendly matches today: Reports, results, goals as Aston Villa lose, Hull win and Everton held by Bolton

Watch highlights as Premier League clubs start pre-season

Last Update:

Premier League clubs continued their preparations for the 2026/27 by playing friendly fixtures on Saturday.

Europa League champions Aston Villa fell to a narrow defeat to Porto in the Portuguese capital, while top-flight newcomers Hull City won comfortably as the build-up to the new campaign continues for the 20 Premier League teams.

Everton, meanwhile, played out a goalless stalemate against Championship opponents.

Table of Contents

Porto vs Aston Villa: Europa League champions narrowly beaten

Aston Villa, last season’s Europa League champions, were beaten 2-1 by Porto in the Portuguese capital.

Having lost Morgan Rogers to Chelsea in a record-breaking transfer for a British player, and with Alejandro Garnacho going the other way on loan, Unai Emery’s men fell behind to a William Gomes goal after just five minutes.

Teenager Luka Lynch then levelled with a fine finish just after the quarter of an hour mark, before Brazilian wide-man Pepe restored the host’s lead.

Aston Villa starting XI: Marco Bizot, Matty Cash, Modou Kéba Cisse, Tyrone Mings, Ian Maatsen, Lamare Bogarde, Ross Barkley, Leon Bailey, Luka Lynch, George Hemmings, Bradley Burrowes

Aston Villa substitutes: James Wright, Joe Gauci, Jamaldeen Jimoh-Aloba, Kosta Nedeljkovic, Joao Gomes, Brian Madjo, Triston Rowe, Aidan Borland, Ben Broggio, Rodrigo Fortes, TJ Carroll

Hull vs Konyaspor: Tigers deliver dominant display in first outing

In their first match of pre-season, Hull ran out comfortable 3-0 winners over their Turkish opposition in Slovenia.

Enis Destan and Abu Kamara scored either side of an own goal to secure a positive result for the newly promoted Premier League outfit.

Oli McBurnie thought he had added further sheen to the scoreline when he made it four but the goal was ruled out for a supposed foul.

Hull City starting XI: Jack Butland, Maty Jacob, Cathal McCarthy, Paddy McNair, Cody Drameh, Darko Gyabi, Oscar Zambrano, Abdulkadir Omur, Ibrahim Akintola, Enis Destan, Abu Kamara

Hull second-half XI: Dillon Phillips, Ryan Giles, John Egan, Semi Ajayi, Lewie Coyle, Matt Crooks, Regan Slater, Kieran Dowell, Liam Millar, Mohamed Belloumi, Oli McBurnie

Bolton vs Everton: Goalless stalemate at the Toughsheet Community Stadium

Everton and Bolton played out a goalless stalemate as the Premier League side were held by their Championship opposition.

After a quiet opening first 15 minutes, Everton had a goal disallowed when Thierno Barry was deemed to have been offside.

Toffees head coach David Moyes made five changes at half-time, introducing Tom King, Michael Keane, Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall, Vitalii  Mykolenko and Tyrique George for Mark Travers, Jarrad Branthwaite, Carlos Alcaraz, Adam Aznou and Harrison Armstrong.

But the changes failed to change the result as neither side could break the deadlock, with the game petering out without much action.

Everton starting XI: Mark Travers, Jarrad Branthwaite, James Tarkowski, Adam Aznou, Jake O’Brien, Merlin Rohl, Tim Iroegbunam, Carlos Alcaraz, Dwight McNeil, Thierno Barry, Harrison Armstrong

Everton substitutes: Tom King, George Pickford, Michael Keane, Beto, Vitalii Mykolenko, Tyrique George, Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall, William Tamen, George Finney, Braiden Graham, Eli Campbell, Malik Olayiwola, Harvey Foster

Premier League pre season fixtures today

Three Premier League clubs are in action later on Saturday and during the early hours of Sunday morning.

When does the 2026/27 Premier League season start?

The campaign starts on the weekend of Friday, August 21. You can see the full list of Premier League fixtures in August and September and TV schedule.

Elsewhere in Europe

Scottish champions Celtic raced into a 2-0 lead inside the opening half-hour of their match against Ruben Amorim’s AC Milan but were eventually pegged back.

New signing Camilo Duran continued his impressive start to life in Glasgow, netting his third goal in as many games to give his new employers the early advantage.

Duran then turned provider, setting up James Forrest who grabbed his side’s second with 28 minutes on the clock.

However, the Serie A side hit back after the break, with Francesco Camarda bagging a brace – the first from the penalty spot – to ensure the former Manchester United’s boss’ side avoided defeat.

In Germany, last season’s runaway Bundesliga winners Bayern Munich fell to a 2-1 defeat to third-tier side Wehen Wiesbaden.

A youthful Bayern team – with an average age of just over 17 years – fell behind when Ibrahim Ati Allah gave the home side the lead in a game to mark the club’s 100th anniversary.

Tom Bischof’s penalty for Vincent Kompany’s side levelled the score before Lukas Schleimer pounced in the closing minutes to give the hists victory.

Elsewhere, Borussia Dortmund were also beaten by the same scoreline in their clash with Dusseldorf.

Seventeen-year-old Mathis Albert gave Dortmund the lead in the first half but goals from Fabian Schleuse and Anas Slimani after the break turned the tie the favour of the third division club.

Meanwhile, Juventus beat Belgian side Standard Liege 1-0 courtesy of a well-worked set-piece.

From a free-kick on the edge of the box, Andrea Cambiaso teed up Fabio Miretti who blasted into the net.

articles.title: Cape Verde hero Vozinha set to join Chilean club Colo Colo
articles.summary: The 40-year-old goalkeeper had a World Cup to remember this summer
articles.content:
Cape Verde hero Vozinha set to join Chilean club Colo Colo

The 40-year-old goalkeeper had a World Cup to remember this summer

Last Update:

Vozinha, the Cape Verde goalkeeper who become something of a sensation at this summer’s World Cup, is set to sign for Chilean club Colo Colo.

The 40-year-old produced a string of memorable saves – most notably in the goalless draw against eventual winners Spain – as World Cup debutants Cape Verde reached the last 32, where they narrowly fell to finalists Argentina after extra-time.

Vozinha, real name Josimar Jose Evora Dias, quickly garnered legendary status, garnering a string of new admirers, not to mention a few dozen million additional Instagram followers.

And now it appears he has found new employers, with Colo Colo club president Anibal Mosa seemingly announcing the deal ahead of the team’s match against Deportes Limache on Friday.

“Vozinha ​will be a Colo Colo player,” Mosa said.

“In the ​coming days he will travel to Chile, undergo the usual medical examinations and then be presented here at the ​Estadio Monumental.”

Although the deal has yet to be finalised, Colo Colo teased the signing on social media with an ​image appearing ​to show ⁠the veteran goalkeeper’s trademark curly hair.

Vozinha, who was voted by fans into the World Cup team of the tournament, had been looking for a new club after his contract with Portuguese second-division side Chaves expired at the end of last season.

It now seems he will join a club widely regarded as the most successful in Chilean football history.
